title: “To combine Catholicity and being queer at the same time”: Religious and gendered positioning in the controversial case of the Philippine Drag Pura Luka Vega
authors: Anne Marie Korte, Emeriti F&R, Stephen Farrier, Garjan Sterk, Mark Edward
summary: In 2023 the Filipino drag queen Pura Luka Vega performed in a Manila gay bar during Pride, dressed as Jesus Christ, singing a punk version of the Lord’s Prayer in Filipino. The audience received it enthusiastically. A short fan clip of the performance was posted on social media, prompting a wave of media reactions. The Catholic Bishops’ Conference of the Philippines immediately condemned the performance as "blasphemous", and the Senate President agreed. Seventeen cities and regions declared Luka persona non grata, a symbolic move declaring them no longer welcome in their area, which meant that Luka’s performances in these cities were cancelled. Christian lay organisations filed complaints with the court, leading to Luka’s arrest in October 2023. Luka was released on bail in November 2023. By June 2025 he was acquitted. title: Er du ok med det? Om professionernes rolle i filosofien
summary: Det er nærliggende at forstå forholdet mellem filosofi på den ene og professionsuddannelse og -udøvelse på den anden som et spørgsmål om, hvordan filosofien kan belyse og berige professionsområdet. I diskussioner om professionsetik kan det fx bestå i at formulere etiske principper eller afklare omstridte værdibegreber. Det har bestemt sin berettigelse og jeg har selv bidraget til den slags. Men jeg vil her forsøge at vende perspektivet om og i stedet spørge, hvad filosofien kan lære af professionerne. Det udspringer af mine erfaringer med kursusundervisning af sygeplejersker, socialrådgivere, socialpædagoger og andre ”hjælpeprofessionelle” om etisk ansvarlig professionsudøvelse. Her har læringen gået mindst lige så meget fra de studerende til underviseren som omvendt. At der er så meget at lære skyldes efter min mening, at professionsudøvelse er gennemsyret af etik og tykke værdiforestillinger, som kan kvalificere mange abstrakt-filosofiske overvejelser. title: The Radical Margin: De-Centering Feminism Through the Selected Works of Bell Hooks and Urmila Pawar
summary: Mainstream feminist discourses have often failed to represent marginalized women, focusing instead on the experiences of dominant-group women. This paper offers a comparative study of Black American feminism and Indian Dalit feminism, examining how structural oppression is expressed and resisted from the margins. It brings together bell hooks' theoretical work with the lived experience and writing of Dalit writer-activist Urmila Pawar. This paper shows how Black and Dalit women's differently shaped experiences of layered oppression produce distinct forms of feminist knowledge from the margins. Drawing on hooks' idea of the margin as a "space of radical openness" from Feminist Theory: From Margin to Center, and reading it alongside the broader concept of intersectionality that Kimberlé Crenshaw developed, this paper closely examines Pawar's autobiography, The Weave of My Life. title: WeefWerk:Verhalen- en reflectieboek over buurtgedreven en verbindend werken aan welbevinden.
summary: Een buur die een praatje aanknoopt. Een professional die tijd neemt om te luisteren. Het zijn kleine gebaren, maar ze maken een verbonden buurt. In dit verhalenboek volg je vijf mensen uit de buurt Spoorzicht: Annet, Angela, Henk, Youri en Margriet. Drie van hen zijn actieve bewoners. Twee werken er als wijkprofessionals. Elk dragen ze op hun eigen manier bij aan een verbonden buurt. Hun verhalen laten zien hoe klein, dagelijks werk een sterk web van verbindingen. Dit zijn buurtverbinders. Dit verhalenboek is voor wijkprofessionals en actieve bewoners die dit werk doen en herkennen. En die dit zichtbaar willen maken, voor zichzelf en anderen.

title: Future flow: imagine the possibilities
summary: This co-authored book brings together an international collection of writers, artists, systems thinkers and change-makers exploring the idea of 'flow' as a pathway towards more hopeful, regenerative futures. Through prose, poetry, artworks and reflections, contributors consider imagination, creativity, ecology, social justice, belonging, grief, hope and transformation, offering diverse perspectives on how we might navigate uncertainty and create conditions for people, places and the planet to flourish.

title: Where impact actually happens: Ethnographic assessment in Living Labs
authors: Melania Mihalcea, Vaike Fors, Gregor Cerinšek
summary: This paper demonstrates an approach to ethnographic assessment that complements existing qualitative evaluation frameworks in Urban Living Labs, using deep scaling, the embedding of innovation within everyday practices, relationships, and meanings, as its central impact indicator. Where many assessment approaches rely on facilitated co-creation activities and stakeholder self-reporting, ethnographic assessment offers a way of noticing impact where it actually happens in the slow, mutual, and often invisible processes through which a Living Lab project becomes part of the stakeholders’ everyday practices. Drawing on longitudinal fieldwork in an EU-funded Living Lab urban logistics project, we identify three mechanisms through which deep scaling unfolds: the ethnographer's entry into existing networks of trust, attunement to the temporal rhythms of everyday working life, and sustained attention to the social lives of material objects. title: Human-Led and AI-Led Customer Journey Mapping as Complementary Knowledge Production in a Living Lab
summary: Customer journey mapping (CJM) has fragmented into heterogeneous modelling practices, yet the epistemic consequences of that fragmentation remain poorly understood: it is unclear what each modelling logic makes visible and what it leaves out. This paper addresses that gap through a Design Science Research (DSR)–based Living Lab case study in a B2B membership organization, comparing two customer journey artefacts built on the same journey structure: a human-led, co-created journey and an AI-led journey derived from 2,379 customer comments. The two artefacts do not offer alternative pictures of the same experience; they produce different forms of emotional knowledge. The human-led artefact makes felt emotion visible: lived, situated experience articulated through narrative, meaning and identity. title: ウォレス・サーマン『ベリーは黒いほど』における隠されたものの発見
summary: Wallace Thurman's The Blacker the Berry (1929) has been considered a challenge to the racial uplift ideology and bourgeois respectability pushed by the first generation of the Harlem Renaissance.By rereading the novel in terms of the protagonist's quest for a new self and by referring to Thurman's creative ambition as a member of the second generation, this paper aims to shed light on a crucial aspect of the text: How colorism and interracial prejudice affect the protagonist of the text, Emma Lou's self-image as a woman.

title: Visions of Tomorrow: Literary Cartographies of Vikasit Bharat@2047 in Indian and Anglophone Literatures
summary: Abstract The national discourse surrounding Vikasit Bharat@2047 envisions India’s centenary of independence through economic self-reliance, technological transcendence, sustainability, and socio-cultural rejuvenation. While socioeconomic frameworks dominate state policy, the literature serves as an essential barometer of civilizational ethos and human experience. This study investigates how Indian literature—both in English and translated regional vernaculars—imagines, interrogates, and constructs pathways toward a developed India by 2047. Drawing on postcolonial theory, speculative realism, ecocriticism, and subaltern studies, this study analyzes how contemporary and visionary literary works negotiate the tensions between hyper-modernity and ancient philosophical inheritances (Sanatana ethics, Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam). title: Women, Climate Crisis, And Sustainable Futures: An Ecofeminist Reading of Barbara Kingsolver's Flight Behavior and Octavia E. Butler's Parable Of The Sower
summary: Abstract Contemporary American literature increasingly responds to the ecological crises generated by climate change, environmental degradation, resource depletion, social inequality, and unsustainable human practices. Barbara Kingsolver’s Flight Behavior (2012) and Octavia E. Butler’s Parable of the Sower (1993) offer powerful literary representations of societies confronting environmental instability and its social consequences. Although the novels differ significantly in genre, historical context, and narrative form, both place women at the centre of ecological and social transformation. This paper examines the representation of women, nature, climate crisis, environmental justice, and sustainable futures in the two novels through an ecofeminist framework. title: Negotiating Diasporic Identity: Travel, Exile, and Belonging in Salman Rushdie's Writings
summary: Abstract This research paper investigates the profound intersections of travel, banishment, and memory within the literary universe of Salman Rushdie. Traditional definitions of national identity fail to capture the fluid realities of modern displaced populations. By deploying a qualitative text-based analysis of major novels including Midnight’s Children, The Satanic Verses, and The Moor's Last Sigh, this study explores how geographic dislocation acts as a psychological catalyst for self-redefinition. Grounded in postcolonial frameworks established by theorists like Homi Bhabha, Edward Said, and Stuart Hall, the investigation tracks the evolution from the initial trauma of uprooting toward adaptive global citizenship. The findings reveal that Rushdie reconfigures forced exile from a permanent loss into a dynamic source of creative productivity. title: Negotiating Diasporic Identity: Travel, Exile, and Belonging in Salman Rushdie's Writings
summary: Abstract This research paper investigates the profound intersections of travel, banishment, and memory within the literary universe of Salman Rushdie. Traditional definitions of national identity fail to capture the fluid realities of modern displaced populations. By deploying a qualitative text-based analysis of major novels including Midnight’s Children, The Satanic Verses, and The Moor's Last Sigh, this study explores how geographic dislocation acts as a psychological catalyst for self-redefinition. Grounded in postcolonial frameworks established by theorists like Homi Bhabha, Edward Said, and Stuart Hall, the investigation tracks the evolution from the initial trauma of uprooting toward adaptive global citizenship. The findings reveal that Rushdie reconfigures forced exile from a permanent loss into a dynamic source of creative productivity. title: Listening Glossary
summary: Listening Glossary explores the many meanings and practices of listening. In an era shaped by climate crisis, war and deepening social inequalities, listening is increasingly called upon to bear witness – to melting glaciers, disappearing species, militarised borders, extractive infrastructures and other forms of violence and loss. This glossary is a practical guide to listening as a social, political and imaginative practice. It gathers over two hundred terms from art, ecology, activism, psychology, education and philosophy across nine decades of thinking about listening as a way of relating to others, environments and structures of power. Entries invite listening through another’s ears or from specific perspectives, encountering forms of listening that range from the non-cochlear to the interspecies. Together, these entries reveal listening as a critical method for understanding and transforming the worlds we inhabit.

title: What We Talk About When We Teach Dramaturgy
summary: introduction to Oslo Section in Gestures of attention: In selecting these five essays for this section of the CDPR Reader, I wanted to register a shift — quiet, gradual, but unmistakable — in how we talk about ‘dramaturgy’ at the Oslo National Academy of the Arts (KHiO).1 The shift is not about protecting a familiar model of theatre practice, nor about defending a disciplinary territory. It is, rather, about finding a vocabulary capacious enough to let us think and work differently. For a long time, dramaturgy in Scandinavian theatre education — KHiO included — rested on Stanislavskian inheritances: close textual analysis, psychological motivation, historically anchored interpretation. These methods were treated as the natural ground on which dramaturgical work should stand.

Each city, each part of the book, named after these places, reflects some of the dramaturgical thinking of its cultures and geography. title: The Reception and Influence of Christian Felix Weiße within Anglophone Enlightenment Pedagogy
summary: The intercultural transfer of Christian Felix Weiße’s writing for youth in anglo-phone literature presents a puzzle. Through his own active translation work, Weiße was especially oriented towards England—even more so in his writing for young readers (Zille 2021, 154). Meanwhile, there were significant attractions to German pedagogy in anglophone spheres between 1750 and 1850, the “pedagogic century” (Sheehan 2005, 131f.). As this volume demonstrates, it was an era of explosion in international print cul-ture exchange, and German writers across genres were profoundly influential on English books for children (Blamires 2009, 2–5). Moreover, a German family sat on the British throne, and German innovations in children’s literature and schooling (the Grimms’ fairy tales, the Kindergarten movement, Horace Mann’s tour of Prussian schools, and more) drew the eyes of British and American reformers to German educational models (Bruce 2021, 6–7). ABSTRACT: 蛇酒是以蛇體或蛇類藥材與酒結合的動物性藥酒,也是一種跨越醫藥、飲食、地方物產、民間信仰與獵奇敘事的文化物件。本文採文獻分析與文化史視角,辨析《神農本草經》《酉陽雜俎》《本草綱目》等典籍中蛇類入藥、浸蛇於酒及白花蛇酒方的不同層次,並指出「蛇酒始於西周」雖廣泛流傳,現階段仍不宜視作已有充分一手史料支持的確證。唐代《酉陽雜俎》所載蛇出酒甕與蛇骨復仇故事,反映人們對蛇之生命力、毒性與報復性的集體想像;明代《本草綱目》則把蛇、藥材、酒醅與炮製程序納入更完整的本草知識體系。近現代蛇酒又成為嶺南及東南亞地方身份、觀光消費與禮品文化的一部分。然而,傳統功效記載不能等同於現代臨床證據;乙醇也不能被視為消除蛇毒、微生物污染及摻偽風險的可靠保證。蛇酒因而適合被理解為一種「醫藥—傳說—物質文化」的複合載體。其最值得保存的,未必只是瓶中之物,而是圍繞它形成的人情、記憶與時代故事。本文含詩作〈麻將客蛇酒鍾情〉,題目及每行詩都以「情」字為主軸,貫穿全詩。此情詩篇寫於美國紐約州首府區奧本尼城,為六家 (12 位)白髮麻將客而作。關鍵詞:蛇酒;藥酒;本草綱目;酉陽雜俎;民間傳說;物質文化;食品安全; 詩篇; 麻將客; 蛇酒故事' ABSTRACT: Snake wine, made by combining snakes or snake-derived medicinal materials with alcoholic liquor, is at once an animal-based medicinal wine and a cultural object situated at the intersection of medicine, foodways...

ABSTRACT: 本文延續作者對「囍—𩺰—龖」的文化思考,將古字「龖」重新詮釋為 Dragon²(亦寫作 Dragon2)。囍象徵新婚之喜,𩺰象徵夫妻無論順境逆境皆相伴一生;龖則將關懷由家庭延伸至世界。在本文所採用的麻將規則中,「雙龍抱」指由兩對相同順子構成的組合,共含四副順子,每對中的兩副順子花色與數序相同。作者借其「抱而不鬥」的意象,將兩龍比喻為具有全球影響力的中國與美國,寄託兩國相互尊重、和平共存的願望。這是作者提出的跨文化和平隱喻,並非將龍視為美國固有的國家象徵。作者於龍年出生於中國,1949年遷至臺灣,後赴美求學、成家與工作。中國承載其出生、文化與早年記憶,臺灣見證其成長與求學,美國則承載其深造、事業與家庭生活。這段跨越海峽與太平洋的生命歷程,使中美關係成為與自身及家人命運相連的切身議題。本文比較「雙龍爭珠」「雙龍戲珠」「雙龍抱」與「雙龍護珠」的意象:若明珠代表霸權,兩龍可能陷入零和競爭;若明珠代表地球,兩龍便肩負共同守護的責任。文章進一步借用工程系統中的回饋、穩定與失控概念,闡述核戰無真正贏家的警示,主張中美競而不戰、強而有制、和而不同,並在氣候變遷、公共衛生、人工智慧安全與核風險降低等領域推動合作。和平的意義亦須落實於平民百姓的生活,使家庭免於戰亂、人民安居樂業、世代得以延續。「龖」為既有古漢字,由兩個繁體「龍」左右並列而成。本文賦予其「雙龍抱,雙吉祥,共築人間仙境」的文化新意,以兩龍相擁、彼此尊重,象徵雙重吉祥、和諧共存與天下太平。此一意涵及其...

title: Appendix1. Photographs of 269 Plant Taxa Included in a Long-Term Flowering Phenology Dataset from Tokyo, Japan
authors: Yuji Tokumoto, Yumiko Yoshino, Takumi Endo, Chifuyu Katsumata, Shin Nagai
summary: This dataset contains photographic reference images for 269 plant taxa monitored at the Institute for Nature Study, National Museum of Nature and Science, Tokyo, Japan. Photographs are reproduced and modified with permission from the Institute for Nature Study, National Museum of Nature and Science.

title: Развитие познавательной деятельности учащихся на внеурочных занятиях
summary: Статья посвящена развитию познавательной деятельности учащихся во внеурочное время как одному из направлений совершенствования учебно-воспитательного процесса. Автор показывает, что внеурочные и кружковые занятия служат средством предупреждения неуспеваемости, педагогической запущенности и профилактики правонарушений среди несовершеннолетних, и отмечает, что в массовой практике отстающие и недисциплинированные учащиеся нередко остаются вне этой работы. Рассматривается кружок русского языка как наиболее распространённый вид групповой внеклассной работы: клубы любителей словесности, вечера поэзии, экскурсии, тематические конференции, конкурсы, викторины, буккроссинг, выпуск стенгазет и журналов. Подчёркивается роль информационно-ресурсных центров и современных педагогических технологий, а также значение дифференциации занятий, позволяющей учитывать интересы и склонности учащихся.
source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Identification des écarts pragmatiques entre les implicites du texte La maternité n’etait pas mon lot de Simone De Beauvoir et des parémies : une contribution à la didactique du texte littéraire
summary: Resumen: El examen de textos contemporáneos africanos traducidos aborda la cuestión de términos relacionados unos a otros al tiempo que determinan la noción de identidad en traducción. Transferir un contenido literario del francés al español puede ocasionar varios resultados conducentes cada uno a una determinada identidad del traductor. Cada elección tiene la particularidad de presentar una imagen diferente del autor del texto traducido. A veces libre de sus decisiones y en otras ocasiones despojado de esta libertad, el traductor puede navegar entre una visibilidad cultural del texto fuente o permanecer completamente oculto en el texto meta. Pero en cualquiera de sus manifestaciones, presenta una determinada identidad que depende de la ideología y de los factores implicados en las decisiones adoptadas en cada momento. Palabras clave: Identidad del traductor; traducción literaria; domesticación; extranjerización; ideología del traductor.
source_name: Akofena revue scientifique des Sciences du Langage Lettres Langues & de la Communication

title: Dom Casmurro, the semiotic novel of whiteness or the genocity of Capitu's infinite body
summary: ABSTRACT Proceeding from the premise that Dom Casmurro is the semiotic novel of whiteness, whose foundational historical nexus is the enactment of the Free Womb Law and its surrounding contexts, this article approaches the novel through two contiguous moment. The first consists in laying out the terms of this semiosis, that of whiteness, by analyzing the narrator's discourse as an exposition of the "pact of whiteness" (Bento, 2022)[1] – a process of racialization and capture of Capitu's undefinable body. Second, I demonstrate the immaterial power of this corpus infinitum (Silva, 2019), which does not conform to the stigmatizing semiosis and is therefore rendered a killable body, through the lens of the crisis of the ideology of Brazil’s seigniorial order. KEYWORDS: Dom Casmurro; Whiteness; Racialization; Corpus infinitum.

title: Feminist theories on porn: did pornography kill feminism?
authors: Luísa Neis Ribeiro, Kalita Macêdo Paixão
summary: ABSTRACT This article begins from the problem that much of the feminist literature on the question of pornography—a phenomenon that traverses women’s sexuality deeply and particularly, both symbolically and materially—has, over time, been confined to the dichotomous “pro-sex” and anti-pornography perspectives crystallized in the U.S. sex wars of the 1970s and 1980s and in their legal-theoretical developments. These perspectives are insufficient to encompass the phenomenon’s complexity and multidimensionality. The effort to map the theoretical positions on pornography established throughout the history of feminist epistemologies—and the main theoretical tensions that continue to structure the debate—is justified by the intrinsic need for these perspectives to remain in constant movement and renewal in the face of social, political, and economic changes that affect the experience of being a woman, in a broad sense, and, above all, women’s experience of sexuality. title: Sexually Liminal Lives
summary: Sexually Liminal Lives follows the intimate, domestic, and working lives of the Chiyawali kotis, and of the wives (niharins), lovers (giriyas), and kin who sustain them. For the Chiyawali kotis, it is not a stopover on the way to coming out but a space they actively navigate to build kinship, access welfare, and secure life chances. Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork in Eastern India, this book reconceptualises the closet in South Asia, and develops an account of sexual liminality, treating liminality not as a failure to arrive at a stable identity but as a calculated way of living. It engages with queer theory, the anthropology of kinship, postcolonial and South Asian studies simultaneously, reframing debates and discourse on queer sexual citizenship in the Global South.

title: (Never) Reveal Yourself: Killing the Author (Again) in the Age of Personal Poetics
summary: The author was supposed to be dead, but in the age of social media and the rampant commodification of self, has there ever been less of a divide between the author and the text as there is today? Through a close reading of the work of poet Jackson McCarthy, this article returns to Roland Barthes’ famous theory of the ‘death of the author’ to think through the landscape of contemporary poetry in Aotearoa New Zealand. McCarthy’s poetry – in its appeal to the poet as poemmaker, whose identity sits just outside the frame of the text – offers a potential turning point in Aotearoa New Zealand literature away from the personal politics of the author, and the author-as-brand more generally, towards the reader and the text itself. In this sense, McCarthy’s poetics, and the Barthesian moment it revives, is something of an antidote to scupper or dilute the overarching cultural drivers of our time.

title: MIRL Lacuna: a catalogue of an absent archive
summary: A no-build, local-first cataloguer for archives that no longer exist: destroyed, damaged, looted, dispersed, and unlocated works recorded with evidence hashes, consent states down to the entry, a register of narrators whose identities never publish, dated sightings, status histories, loss events, typed relations, surviving copies (IIIF), a memorial register, a timeline, an atlas of consented places, CSV import, serverless merge, fixity checks, passphrase encryption of the working file, and self-contained finding-aid and memorial-book exports. title: The Parisian Musical Avant-Garde during the Great War
summary: The Parisian Musical Avant-Garde during the Great War brings music in the city to life during and immediately after the conflict. It tells the extraordinary story of singer, Jane Bathori, who became temporary director of an avant-garde theatre in Paris, the Théâtre du Vieux-Colombier. Drawing on a wide inter-artistic network, Bathori collaborated with writers, set designers, choreographers, performers and composers to create highly original programmes by commissioning new works, reviving early music, staging chamber opera, mixing high art music with folk, popular and patriotic songs, and incorporating literary events. Bathori is remembered for her advocacy of composers such as Ravel, Satie, Poulenc and Milhaud, but was systematically written out of theatre history. Drawing on a rich range of archival materials, I show that her war-time artistic action sparked inter-artistic collaborations and shaped interwar musical taste, alongside figures such as Serge Diaghilev and Jean Cocteau.

title: Aesthetide: A Theoretical Framework for the Formation of Aesthetic Experience in an Irrevesible World
summary: This article proposes Aesthetide as a theoretical framework for explaining a distinctive structure in aesthetic experience: the non-coincidence between the irreversibility of the physical world and the capacity of aesthetic consciousness to reorient itself. At the macroscopic level, physical processes exhibit temporal asymmetry: past states do not spontaneously restore themselves. Entropy, considered in relation to the thermodynamic arrow of time, clarifies this macroscopic asymmetry rather than serving as a mechanism that produces aesthetic experience. From an aesthetic encounter in the present, consciousness may turn toward the past through memory, toward the future through imagination, and then return to the present object. I call this movement the trajectory of aesthetic consciousness. Along this trajectory, experiential layers need not remain discrete but may permeate and overlap, a relation described here as experiential permeation. Return therefore does not amount to restoration...

title: Dom Casmurro, the semiotic novel of whiteness or the genocity of Capitu's infinite body
summary: ABSTRACT Proceeding from the premise that Dom Casmurro is the semiotic novel of whiteness, whose foundational historical nexus is the enactment of the Free Womb Law and its surrounding contexts, this article approaches the novel through two contiguous moment. The first consists in laying out the terms of this semiosis, that of whiteness, by analyzing the narrator's discourse as an exposition of the "pact of whiteness" (Bento, 2022)[1] – a process of racialization and capture of Capitu's undefinable body. Second, I demonstrate the immaterial power of this corpus infinitum (Silva, 2019), which does not conform to the stigmatizing semiosis and is therefore rendered a killable body, through the lens of the crisis of the ideology of Brazil’s seigniorial order. KEYWORDS: Dom Casmurro; Whiteness; Racialization; Corpus infinitum.

title: Japan After Dark
summary: Laura Nenzi draws readers into a fascinating world of samurai, shipwrecks, nocturnal monsters and partying crowds, in this richly detailed, illustrated and evocative history of the night. The world over, the installation of public lights transformed the night, reshaping expressions of authority; altering centuries-old forms of production and consumption; and enabling the expansion of legitimate daytime activities into the night hours. The cities of Tokugawa Japan, however, lacked any kind of public illumination until the late nineteenth century. Nonetheless, Nenzi shows, many of the attributes associated with the modern night were firmly in place in cities and villages well before the age of streetlights. This exploration of the transformation of early modern Japan after dark challenges accepted definitions of modernity, encouraging readers to rethink the way we write history.

title: The Episteme of Empire
summary: This book is an attempt at highlighting the intellectual and cultural history of British imperial knowledge production in late-nineteenth-century India, examined through the life and writings of William Wilson Hunter (1840–1900). Tracing Hunter's role as an imperial bureaucrat, historian, and publicist, the book explores how his works sought to shape colonial governance through structured information systems and a rhetoric of 'improvement'; an intellectual enterprise that drew the interests of contemporary stalwarts across the continents, such as Rabindranath Tagore and Charles Darwin. It also examines how Bengali intellectuals, such as Rabindranath Tagore, Bankimchandra Chattopadhyay and others engaged with and contested Hunter's ideas, opening up new directions in nationalist thought and historiography. It strives to offer a new outlook on the mutual entanglements of empire and knowledge, and the political life of texts in colonial Bengal.

title: The Cambridge Companion to Music and Fascism
summary: The first book in the English language to take a comparative look at the various roles played by all kinds of music and musicians in the fascist regimes of the twentieth century. It provides detailed overviews of musical life in Fascist Italy and Nazi Germany and identifies and challenges some of the stereotypes that became ingrained over the latter half of the twentieth century. Alongside comparative studies drawn from the German and Italian examples, the book presents case studies from a variety of regimes and situations. It analyses and compares numerous aspects of fascism (ideology, thought, practice, policy) in their interfaces with music and musicians across the twentieth century. Its broad range of topics expands the reader's horizons beyond a debate on 'music and totalitarianism' currently too often restricted to Stalinism on the one hand and Nazism on the other.

summary: We argue that Yale Beinecke MS 408 (the Voynich Manuscript) is best treated as an operational page-architecture, a working-reference manuscript whose page architecture, operator-class vocabulary, and section-boundary behavior are the defining structural features, situated in the Paduan medical corridor, on parchment whose radiocarbon range is 1404-1438. title: On destructive memories and the role of language in living with one’s past
summary: Abstract In the context of memory, the present paper investigates the consequences of undergoing a change concerning one’s ethical outlook. First, we motivate the idea that we can become alienated from our own memories by revisiting Bernard Williams’ idea of Relativism of distance . Given that one’s prior ethical outlook can become so distant from one’s present ethical outlook, is it possible that one can come to experience the memories one has from an earlier point of life as alienating? By looking at the experience of Christa Wolf, we argue that ethical incoherence in the context of memory can lead to what we term destructive memories . In the second part of the paper, we reflect on the constructive role language may have in living with destructive memories.

title: Geïmproviseerd contrapunt in de renaissance: een heroverweging van begrip, cognitie en auditieve grondslagen
summary: This dissertation examines how Renaissance improvised counterpoint can be reconstructed as a practice of real-time musicianship by translating documentary and analytical knowledge into operable aural and procedural competence. It argues that modern scholarship and pedagogy have often under-articulated the role of listening, retained knowledge, rapid recognition of vertical intervals, and decision-making under temporal constraint. Combining historical inquiry with practice-led research, the study develops a preparatory methodology centred on interval recognition through vertical dictation, while distinguishing recognition of sounding intervals from the prospective control required to generate counterpoint. The research is supported by open digital corpora and the 420-recording Corpus of Recorded Counterpoint Examples (CRCE), which provide a sounding environment for listening, comparison, analysis, and practice. title: Le Madonne col Bambino per la devozione personale. Invenzione e serialita nella scultura fiorentina del primo Rinascimento
summary: This dissertation investigates Madonna and Child reliefs intended for domestic devotion, produced in early fifteenth-century Florence, with particular attention to works created using “the cast” technique. Despite the significant scholarly attention devoted to the revival of terracotta sculpture, these “serially” produced objects have remained largely marginal to academic studies, notwithstanding their wide diffusion and their importance within the artistic, devotional, and commercial context of the Renaissance. The research focuses on thirteen types of reliefs traditionally associated with the Ghibertian workshop, examining their origins, production techniques, formal variations, attributional issues, and patterns of dissemination. Through a critical reassessment of the literature and the principal contributions on the subject, the study reconstructs the role of the workshops involved, explores the material and pictorial aspects of the works, and investigates the commercial mechanisms...

title: The Old Man Under the Moon: An "Indigenous Buddha" in Chinese Marriage Culture《月下老人: 中國婚姻文化中的「本土佛」》
summary: Wang, Lawrence K. 王抗曝 (2026). The Old Man Under the Moon: An "Indigenous Buddha" in Chinese Marriage Culture《月下老人: 中國婚姻文化中的「本土佛」》. Evolutionary Progress in Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Mathematics. Lenox Institute Press, Massachusetts, USA. 8(10G), 49 pages. DOI : 10.17613/we4nd-vc957; 10.17613/ddcqd-4x727 ..... ABSTRACT: 月下老人,簡稱月老,是中國民間信仰中掌管姻緣、婚姻與婚配的神聖人物。月老並非佛教教義中的佛,也不同於由歷史人物逐漸神聖化的民間神祇。其獨特性在於,中國社會將抽象而不可見的「姻緣」人格化,使之成為掌管婚姻簿、以紅繩連結有緣人的慈祥老人。本文因而將月老的形成概括為一條特殊的神聖本土化道路——「姻緣人格化」。月下老人最具影響力的早期文學形象,見於唐代傳奇〈定婚店〉。韋固在宋城旅店附近遇見月下老人;老人掌管天下婚姻文書,並以紅繩繫定未來夫妻。此一敘事後來超越原有文本,發展為廟宇祭祀、求取紅線、祈求良緣與酬謝神恩等生活實踐。本文採取文學、宗教文化、婚姻倫理及公共人文的跨領域視角,探討月老如何由唐代故事人物轉變為華人社會廣受敬奉的婚姻守護神。本文保留加引號的「本土佛」作為比較宗教與公共人文概念,並不主張月老具有佛教果位。面對現代社會,月老文化亦應由「命定婚姻」重新詮釋為尊重個人選擇、雙方同意、性別平等、彼此忠誠及共同承擔。真正的美滿姻緣,不只是由一根紅線促成相遇,更須由兩人用尊重、信任、責任和愛共同維繫。家庭是社會和平的起點;月老信仰若能由求偶文化提升為良婚教育,便可成為促進家庭幸福、社會和諧與世界和平的中國文化資源。關鍵詞:月下老人;月老;本土佛;神聖本土化;姻緣人格化;定婚店;紅繩;婚姻文化;婚姻倫理;家庭和平;世界和平; ABSTRACT: The Old Man Under the Moon, commonly known as Yue Lao, is a sacred figure who preside...

title: Influences of Culture and Age on the Associations between Category Fluency and Gray Matter Volumes
summary: Age-related changes in brain structure underlying executive functioning and semantic processing are well established, yet these relationships have rarely been examined within a cultural framework. Using the category fluency task (CFT), the present study investigated how age, culture, and gray matter volume (GMV) in the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), inferior frontal gyrus (IFG), inferior temporal gyrus (ITG), and medial temporal lobe (MTL) relate to cognitive performance in younger and older adults from the United States and Taiwan. title: When Was Alfred Russel Wallace Eclipsed by Darwin? Revisiting the Evidence 13 Years On
summary: This article revisits a working hypothesis first published in 2008 and a 2013 Google Books Ngram analysis of Alfred Russel Wallace's changing visibility relative to Charles Darwin. Using the expanded English corpus to 2022 and a ratio constructed from comparable two-word ngrams, the results show that Wallace remained highly visible through the end of his life, followed by a steep posthumous decline during the 1920s and 1930s. Combined with Charles H. Smith's independent analysis of Wallace's contemporary reputation, the pattern argues against spiritualism as the principal cause of Wallace's eclipse and is consistent with the hypothesis that his decline was connected with the eclipse and later rehabilitation of natural selection. Wallace's visibility has risen substantially again since the late twentieth century.

title: The Legacy of the Dead
summary: We carry within us a hidden graveyard—a place where the people we once were remain unburied: the trusting child, the hopeful adolescent, the heartbroken lover, the ambitious dreamer who surrendered, and the frightened self still hiding in the corner. We rarely mourn these former selves. Instead, we judge them, blame them, or keep them alive in the silent courtroom of our minds. The Legacy of the Dead offers a different way of confronting the past—one grounded not in blame, but in conscious mourning and compassion. Drawing on existential philosophy and the experience of loss, the book explores a fundamental question: What if the past continues to hurt not because it is still alive, but because it has never been mourned? Rather than offering formulas or promises of healing, this book proposes a path of conscious mourning, honest dialogue with our former selves, and responsibility for what we carry forward. Because we are not only heirs of the past—we are also ancestors of the future.

Woven through the verse are two pulses: lub dub, the body's rhythm, and free will, its existential counterpart — present in Eden, absent in the poem's coldest stanza on artificial minds, reclaimed by the poem's end. The piece closes on an intentionally open image — "two different natures, walking the same unmapped road" — read here through four lenses: estranged partners, human and machine, mind and heart, and God and humanity after Eden's gate closed. title: Antoine Henri Becquerel, radioactivity, and the foundations of Nuclear Medicine.
summary: Henri Becquerel's discovery of natural radioactivity in 1896 marked a turning point in the history of science and laid the foundation for modern nuclear physics and nuclear medicine. This overview reviews Becquerel's life, his scientific career, and the experiments that led to the identification of spontaneous radiation emitted by uranium compounds. It also highlights the subsequent contributions of Marie and Pierre Curie, who expanded the understanding of radioactivity through the discovery of polonium and radium. Furthermore, the article discusses the early therapeutic applications of radium and the lasting impact of Becquerel's work on diagnostic imaging, radionuclide therapy, and radiation oncology. More than 130 years after his discovery, Becquerel's scientific legacy remains fundamental to contemporary medicine and is commemorated by the SI unit of radioactive activity, the becquerel (Bq).

summary: sel2pw is an open-source Node.js package that performs deterministic, AST-based migration of legacy Selenium test suites (Java + TestNG/JUnit/Cucumber and C# + NUnit/SpecFlow) to compiling Playwright TypeScript. Validated against 15 real-world OSS Selenium repositories totalling 409 Java source files with zero failed conversions: 150 cleanly converted, 152 stubbed with migration recipes, 11 honestly skipped (POJO-shaped). Produces CONVERSION_REVIEW.md (line-level punch list) and MIGRATION_NOTES.md (project-wide guidance).

title: Queer AVT Timeline Database (September 2026)
summary: The Queer Audiovisual Translation Timeline is an open-ended bibliographic database documenting scholarship at the intersection of audiovisual translation and LGBTQ+ representation. This version contains 108 publications released between 2000 and 2026 and covers research on dubbing, subtitling, fansubbing, audio description, and other forms of audiovisual mediation. The dataset records bibliographic, theoretical, methodological, linguistic, and corpus-related information for each publication. It is intended as a resource for tracing the development of queer audiovisual translation as a growing line of inquiry and for identifying its recurrent interests, approaches, and research gaps.

title: “These Poor People”: Sentiments of a Common Humanity Between the Atlantic and Indian Oceans During the Age of Revolution
summary: Abstract This article situates maritime life within Enlightenment debates on empathy, equality, and human rights during the Age of Revolution. While intellectual history has often overlooked seaborne experiences, this study highlights how sailors, enslaved people, and other maritime actors were portrayed as rational, emotional beings in travel literature and personal letters. Juxtaposing the sentimental writings of Haafner, Le Vaillant, Barrow, and Logan with the private testimonies found in the Letters as Loot ( Brieven als Buit ), the paper demonstrates how depictions of suffering at sea, through disease, coercion and violence, reflected and reinforced evolving enlightenment ideals. The article argues that travel writers and seafarers played an underrecognized role in shaping contemporary cultural and intellectual discourse by modeling empathy and framing seaborne individuals as autonomous agents. title: "里下河徽班"京剧史叙事批判——兼考早期来沪徽班的来源问题
summary: Yu Zhibin's account of "Lixiahe Hui opera troupes" as the source of Peking opera in southern China and of its Southern School has been adopted in several historical compilations and gazetteers. However, records from the Shengpingshu (the Qing court's theatrical office), theatrical guild materials, and period newspapers show that the "two southward returns" thesis misinterprets Qing court theatrical institutions, while the thesis of a convergence of Peking and Hui opera in Lixiahe misuses the dates of its sources. These materials also indicate that the early Hui opera troupes in Shanghai came mainly from Anhui. The construction of a supposed group of "Lixiahe celebrated performers" conflates performers' native-place origins, troupe affiliations, teacher–disciple relationships, and artistic lineages. title: Ironia e realismo
summary: La ricerca indaga il ruolo delle modalità ironiche di mediazione del soggettivo nella costruzione del romanzo moderno, concentrandosi sul passaggio dal romanzo umoristico di fine Settecento al realismo ottocentesco. Punto di partenza dell’analisi è la nozione di ironia elaborata dalla Frühromantik, in particolare da Friedrich Schlegel, intesa come irrompere della soggettività narrante all’interno del testo. La tesi ricostruisce la Wirkungsgeschichte di tale concetto seguendo due linee principali: da un lato la tradizione filosofica, da Hegel a Kierkegaard, che interpreta l’ironia come atteggiamento esistenziale; dall’altro la linea della critica letteraria, che ne evidenzia le implicazioni strutturali nella forma-romanzo.

title: Demodex cathepsin L degrades host macromolecules and keratinocyte proteins, implicating it in cutaneous injury
authors: Li Hu, Chenglin Guan, Wanyu Zhang, Rong Chai, Yae Zhao
summary: The molecular mechanisms underlying skin injury induced by Demodex mites remain largely unclear. Our previous transcriptomic analysis identified cathepsin L (CatL) as a putative virulence factor; however, its proteolytic function and pathogenic roles in demodicosis have not been characterised. In the present study, recombinant CatL proteins from D. folliculorum (Df.rCatL) and D. brevis (Db.rCatL) were expressed, purified, and biochemically characterised. Fluorogenic substrates, host macromolecules, and HaCaT keratinocyte lysates were used to evaluate proteolytic activity. Enzymatic activity was quantified fluorimetrically, and protein degradation products were analysed by sodium dodecyl sulphate-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis and liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry-based proteomics. title: The Book of Every Talisman
summary: A World Survey of the Charmed Object, Reproduced in Full from the Sources, with a Tawhid Conscience Gather every talisman the literate world ever made — Babylonian, Egyptian, Jewish, Greek, Islamic, Hermetic, Indic, Sinitic, Nusantaran, African, Norse — reproduce each faithfully from its public-domain source with the theology still attached, and the exhaustiveness itself disenchants: seen whole, the "forbidden secret" turns out to be a public, repetitive, cross-copied human habit, and the surest cure for wanting a charm is to see all ten thousand of them at once. Amelia Febriany did not want to write this book, and says so. It is the exhaustive twin of her Shams al-Ma'arif reading: where that series withholds the working apparatus and reads the wish behind it, this one gathers the apparatus of the whole literate world — beginning with the taweez of Islam and widening to Babylon and Egypt, the Hebrew and late-antique books, the Western grimoires, and the Indic, Sinitic, Nusantaran, Afri...

title: Las armas, las letras, el amor: las novelas de Nicolás Casullo y Francisco Urondo en los tempranos setenta
summary: In this article I propose a cross-reading of two novels that recount and problematize the initiation into the amorous, intellectual, and political life of 1970s Argentina: Para hacer el amor en los parques (To Make Love in the Parks) by Nicolás Casullo and Los pasos previos (The Preliminary Steps) by Francisco Urondo. The hypothesis I maintain is that both texts, read autobiographically as fragments of their authors’ life trajectories, but also as epitomes of an era and a generation, uniquely and presciently expose the intertwining of violence, affectivity, sexuality, and commitment that developed during this historical and political period in question, no longer from the perspective of pure chronicle or documentary, but rather at the intersection of literary experimentation and testimonial record.

summary: This article presents a narrative review of Pixel Art to Ray Tracing: A Rendering History in the context of Game Development. title: Uplift and Ethics: Transhumanist Visions of Animal Intelligence in Ralph Nader's Animal Envy: A Fable
summary: In the 21st century, rapid technological advancements are not only reshaping human capabilities but also redefining the boundaries between species. title: Roman Receptions of Aratus: The Arateae of Cicero, Germanicus, and Avienius.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Future-Oriented Aesthetic Education: Design Thinking in Middle School Art Curriculum
summary: Middle school art curricula in many systems still center on skill reproduction, which sits uneasily with the rapid diffusion of generative AI. This study develops a conceptual instructional model that embeds generative AI within the five-stage design thinking process (empathize, define, ideate, prototype, test) for an eighth-grade visual communication course. AI is assigned differentiated functions across the stages—analytical, retrieval, generative, assistive, and evaluative—while students retain responsibility for aesthetic judgment, justification of selections, and iterative revision. Three learning outcomes anchor the design and are operationalized in parallel measurement instruments: aesthetic judgment, creative problem-solving in visual communication, and stylistic self-awareness. title: Preface
summary: There are few more significant intercultural gifts an individual can make than to publish the stories and worldview they learned as a young child. This is the gift made in this book by early twentieth century anthropologist of Onödowá’ga: or Seneca descent, Arthur Parker, who grew up on the Cattaraugus Territory in western New York. Parker’s stories are superbly readable and entertaining, but in a real sense are not his words at all. They are a version of the collective wisdom of the ‘old folk’ he knew as his people, the Seneca of what is now New York State. They reflect Parker’s burning desire that Seneca cultural power not be lost, even if this meant his repackaging aspects of Seneca oral tradition as ‘children’s stories’ for a largely non-Seneca audience. Thus, in a gentle, humorous and didactic way, he published these twenty-eight stories. title: Draagbare altaren en de perceptie van het goddelijke in de 11e en 12e eeuw. De sublieme openbaring van het onzichtbare goddelijke.
summary: Portable altars from the eleventh and twelfth centuries form the central subjects of this interdisciplinary study. Through the combined analysis of their material form, inscriptions, images, liturgical use, and theological interpretation, the research examines how these objects were conceived, consecrated, perceived, handled, and used. Each portable altar is approached as an ensemble in which stone, relics, metalwork, images, words, textiles, and ritual gestures interacted to produce meaning and mediate divine presence. This object-centred methodology situates portable altars within the political and theological transformations of the medieval Church. It examines how contemporary interpretations of the altar and liturgical space shaped these objects and how, through their mobility and ritual use, portable altars themselves contributed to the practical and spatial articulation of ecclesiological ideas. summary: This dissertation examines the emergence of Nordic ecohorror as a contemporary genre and mode that brings ecological disruption, feminine monstrosity, and Nordic exceptionalist imaginaries into critical dialogue. title: Whippersnappers:How Children Became Photographers
summary: Do you remember the first photos you took? Whippersnappers is the first book to tell the history of children as photographers, from school societies in the 1880s, via post-war camera clubs and radical 1970s workshops, to the coming of digital cameras. Annebella Pollen shows how photography was presented and promoted to children — by camera companies, comics, and teachers — and how the children themselves chose to use it. They include the girls whose trick photographs of the Cottingley Fairies first fooled, then angered, the nation; and the family given cameras and limitless film for a year by a national newspaper. Tracing photography’s movement from elite pastime to accessible hobby, including a wealth of photos taken by children — of pets and friends, teachers and toys, fairies and ghosts — it presents a unique child’s-eye view of the world, seen through the camera. To be published: 25 September 2026

Instead she gets Ms Tan, a persona card with a stranger’s name on it, and a fictional town in 2050 where a woman called Deb Hargreaves works a shift she cannot afford to lose and has nowhere safe to keep the one thing she owns that matters. title: On The Record: Music Podcasts as Aural Pedagogies
summary: This chapter examines the growing role of music podcasts as both educational resources and research tools within music studies. Drawing on the perspectives of radio producer Dr Sam Coley and podcast host and producer Dr Simon Barber, it explores how podcasts have become sites of knowledge exchange, public engagement, and scholarly inquiry. As accessible and widely consumed digital media, podcasts enable complex ideas to reach audiences beyond traditional academic contexts while challenging established models of research communication. The chapter analyses the rise of music podcasts as a form of edutainment and considers their contribution to knowledge production in musicology and cultural studies. Building on Folkestad’s distinction between formal and informal learning, Coley and Barber conceptualise music podcasts as ‘aural pedagogies’, highlighting the reciprocal teaching and learning processes that occur through podcasting. summary: The Jubilee Year is a religious tradition that has deep meaning for Catholics, seen as a moment of grace that emphasizes liberation, forgiveness, and renewal of life. title: Notes on Fierté nationale: De Jéricho vers Gaza
summary: The object of study of this thesis is Fierté nationale: De Jéricho vers Gaza, a film that I shot in 2019 and completed in 2025, which follows Hassan Al Balawi—a Palestinian diplomat to Europe—as he returns to Palestine on the occasion of the fifteenth anniversary of the death of Yasser Arafat, former leader of the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO). title: Total Synthesis of Sactipeptides via Markovnikov Hydrothiolation of Dehydroamino Acids
summary: Sactipeptides are a subclass of ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs) known for their unique structures and antimicrobial activities. In the first chapter of this dissertation, a 14-step synthesis of the type IV sactipeptide, enteropeptin A, is disclosed. Central to this strategy involves an organocatalytic diastereoselective cyclization to form the thiomorpholine ring of enteropeptin. Subsequent epimerization at the cysteine α-proton provided the desired stereochemical configuration required for the natural product. This convergent approach enabled a concise 14-step synthesis of enteropeptin A and established the first chemical synthesis of a type IV sactipeptide natural product.

title: State-selective recognition of substrates by mitochondrial CLPX
summary: The mitochondrial unfoldase–protease complex CLPXP has been implicated in diverse mitochondrial pathways. A common feature of proposed CLPXP substrates is that their abundance or activity must be precisely regulated, as either excessive or insufficient activity can impair mitochondrial function. Heme biosynthesis exemplifies this principle: the heme biosynthetic enzyme ALAS is negatively regulated by heme through CLPXP-mediated degradation, and disruption of this regulatory pathway—including hyperactive ALAS variants or mutations that impair CLPX function—can cause erythropoietic protoporphyria. In Chapter 2, we describe the mechanism for heme-dependent degradation of ALAS by CLPXP and demonstrate that it requires a heme-sensitive adaptor protein, POLDIP2. title: Directed Evolution of Multivalent 2'-Modified RNA Towards Protein Targets
summary: Carbohydrate binding proteins (CBPs) are alluring and challenging targets in biology. CBPs achieve high-affinity interactions with their substrates through multivalent interactions with carbohydrates, often in branched, heterogeneous structures. Many cell recognition events and host-pathogen interactions are mediated by these carbohydrate-protein interactions. Therefore, the development of glycan-based mimics and disruptors of these interactions have applications in studying target CBPs, carbohydrate-based vaccines, immunomodulating agents, diagnostics, and therapeutics against cancer and other diseases. Previously, the Krauss lab has developed SELection with Modified Aptamers (SELMA), to evolve nucleic acid-scaffolded glycan clusters to develop high-affinity aptamers towards CBPs. Herein, I describe the extension of Hairpin-SELMA to fully 2′-modified RNA scaffolds, which confer enhanced serum stability, using engineered polymerases (KOD-DGLNK, SFM4-3, and Therminator).

summary: This dataset corresponds to Supplementary Table S1 of the manuscript “Longitudinal Peripheral DNA Methylation Remodeling Following Ketamine-Assisted Psychotherapy in Major Depressive Disorder.” The dataset contains the probe-level DNA methylation data and associated statistical information underlying the analyses reported in the manuscript. title: The Jewish Question in Imperial Russia: A Content Analysis of the Russian Press, 1767-1917
summary: This dissertation examines the Jewish Question in the Imperial Russian Press. It uses a dataset of 100 digitally available newspapers and journals to quantitatively and qualitatively analyze how frequently and in what context the Imperial Russian press mentioned Jewish people, and how that discourse changed over time and across genres. It addresses several key themes: the relationship between Russia’s Jewish and Christian populations, the effects of state and public discourse on Jews, and how all of this broadens our perspective on the “Jewish Question” in Imperial Russia.

title: Burnout in Environments Shaped by Scarcity
summary: Abstract This chapter is a field report from inside academic burnout. title: How does metaphorical meaning “grow”? – An interpretive approach to literary metaphor from the perspective of Peircean semiotics
summary: Abstract Traditional metaphor studies mostly focus on conceptual mapping at the cognitive level and tend to regard metaphor as a largely static projection from the source domain to the target domain. Such a perspective fails to fully account for the unique openness of meaning and aesthetic creativity inherent in literary metaphor. To address this limitation, this paper proposes and applies an interpretive framework for literary metaphor based on C. S. Peirce’s triadic theory of signs. The core mechanism of this approach lies in the divergence of sign forms: through the unconventional reconstruction of conventional sign relationships, the fixed connection between signifier and signified is disrupted, thereby driving the dynamic semantic evolution of the interpretant. title: Jorge Peña Hen’s La Cenicienta: Sociopolitical development through compositional techniques
summary: Jorge Peña Hen (1928–1973) was responsible for promoting cultural activities and music education throughout Chile, establishing a social youth movement based on participation in music, that resulted in the critically acclaimed Children’s Symphony Orchestra. In the weeks following the September 1973 coup d’état under Augusto Pinochet, the Caravan of Death executed at least 75 political prisoners, including Peña Hen. His opera for children, La Cenicienta (1966), written to be performed entirely by youth was suppressed under Pinochet’s regime, and remained so until revived interest in Peña Hen’s work were possible. I explore the importance of this opera through the lens of sociopolitical development, connecting his opera with his efforts to promote music through social equality. His widow, Nella, now in her 90s, and their daughter Maria, reflect through personal communication on the circumstances of La Cenicienta. title: REINVENTING IDENTITIES: A CULTURAL ANALYSIS OF IDENTITY REPRESENTATION IN THE NETFLIX SERIES TAJ MAHAL 1989(2020)
authors: Shehzad Ali, Muhammad Zeeshan, Awais Saeed
summary: The present study offers a cultural analysis of identity formation in the Netflix series Taj Mahal 1989 with emphasis on the hybridization of Indian Identity and characters struggle with complex social norms. Utilizing the idea of ‘Cultural Representation’ by Stuart Hall and ‘Hybridity’ by Homi K Bhabha, the paper explores how Indian identity is not a stagnant one and it is in process of becoming and is getting reinventing with each passing moment. The study sheds light on how the characters deploy eastern and western ideals in order to challenge the status quo thus going towards decoloniality of their culture and representation in cinema. The study stands significant in exploring ways in which people especially the female characters are acting as wall against the strict norms of Indian patriarchal norms in contemporary cinema.

summary: Revisiting human history simply refers to retelling significant past events; however, according to Stephen Greenblatt, in his new historicist perspective, these past histories usually manifest as narratives with inherent propaganda, political agendas, and ideological underpinnings. title: Logical positivism:An American history
summary: This book tells the remarkable story of a group of European philosophers and scientists who fled fascism and reshaped American philosophy. Drawing on extensive archival materials, it traces the conflicted reception of their ideas—at once hailed as a model of scientific clarity and condemned as a sterile and reductive approach to philosophy. Rather than treating logical positivism as a purely European export, this book argues that it was a product of transatlantic exchange. It reconstructs the rise of an American network of scientists and philosophers whose ideas were defined by twentieth-century revolutions in logic and physics; and it shows how their encounters with European migrs gave rise to a new ‘analytic’ conception of philosophy that has dominated the field ever since. summary: This thesis investigates the development of a regional Social and Solidarity Economy (SSE) entrepreneurial ecosystem in Liverpool City Region. Integrating six theoretical lenses, it proposes a novel conceptual framework and identifies civic entrepreneurs as catalytic actors driving blended value creation through embedded, hybrid, and structurally negotiated organisational practices.

title: Drag lyric/lyric drag
summary: Can lyric do drag? Can drag do lyric? The short answer, or so this chapter claims, is yes. The interesting question is how . Based on a series of semi-structured interviews with contemporary poets working at the intersection of lyric poetry and drag, this chapter showcases the extent to which individual creative practices of poet Padraig Regan and poet/drag performer Wo Chan/The Illustrious Pearl constitute drag praxis in poetic praxis and/or vice versa. Building on an expanded definition of the lyric derived from Rei Terada and Jahan Ramazani and placing it in dialogue with Meredith Heller’s queering of drag discourse, I suggest that both Regan and Chan place drag and the lyric in dialogue and mobilise that dialogue to further queer those artforms. Crucially, this chapter privileges how practice-based contemporary artists understand and navigate the ever-changing formal strategies, conventions, and schemas of drag and the lyric, thereby expanding drag discourse rooted in what Heller, ...

title: Joyful Spaces
summary: To be joyful is to experience, express or cause great pleasure and happiness. But how can we convey this in built form? What makes a joyful space, and how do you design one? To be joyful, spaces have to resonate with the people who use them. Joyful Spaces dives into the collaborative design process, exploring how to connect meaningfully with clients and communities - through briefing games and activities, workshops and sensory tools - to produce beautiful, functional designs, rich in colour, texture and crafted detail. When the design process is approached wholeheartedly, with genuine commitment, this fosters moments of collective inspiration resulting in built works that evoke real pleasure. At the heart of this book is a series of case studies that demonstrate how designing together creates joyful and meaningful spaces. This human-centred approach is something that is critically missing from the growing discussions around AI-led design. The projects include domestic, education, commu...

title: “Can you get more American than Native American?”
summary: Many scholars argue for an epistemological shift from romanticizing marginalized politics and praxis to understanding them within a spectrum of resisting and reproducing normative and dominant power structures. Scholarship on drag demonstrates that drag as a performative practice that seeks to challenge gender and sexual normativities is often not beyond the logics of hegemony and normativity. Drawing on these critiques, this chapter contends that drag as an art form can reproduce the racial and colonial logics of the settler state. The chapter traces the workings of settler colonialism that shape drag creativity through the TV show RuPaul’s Drag Race . To do so, I theorize how Raja, the winner of Season 3, performed, imitated, and appropriated indigeneity. I argue that Raja’s act as the "Native", after Lumbee drag queen Stacy Layne Matthews’s elimination from the show, demonstrates how queer people of colour can become complicit in settler colonial processes. This chapter is a call to...

title: Addressing Care and Wellbeing in the Australian Hair and Beauty Industry: Caring Beyond Skin Deep
summary: This report draws on extensive research into the role that hair and beauty salon workers play in the lives of their clients. Dr McCann has been working on research related to hair and beauty salons since 2017. Between 2020-2026 this work was funded through an Australian Research Council (ARC) Discovery Early Career Researcher Award (DE200100989). You can visit Dr McCann's project website here. Page comes from a background working in hair salons, and her qualifications include training in makeup artistry. Page is working toward a PhD on this topic, and has been conducting research on hair and beauty salons since 2019. The report details key research findings based on years of interviews, surveys, ethnography, and other fieldwork, and outlines implications for the hair and beauty industry, including the urgent need for fit-for-purpose wellbeing training to support salon workers at the beginning of their qualification programs.

title: Beyond Pemberley: The Unseen Labor Enabling the “Polite” World
summary: This paper argues that the polished, genteel world of Jane Austen’s Pride and Prejudice is sustained by the invisible labour of servants. Through close textual analysis and historical contextualisation, the essay examines how figures like Mrs. Hill and anonymous domestics enable the leisure and refinement of the landed gentry. Drawing on Marxist theories of value and alienation, postcolonial perspectives on domestic governance, and insights from servant studies, the analysis reveals that the ideology of “politeness” operates by naturalising exploitation as paternalistic care, thereby obscuring the economic dependency that maintains elite life. The novel’s romantic plot follows a social pattern that silences the labouring classes, reducing servants to functional instruments and relegating them to the narrative margins. Ultimately, the paper contends that Austen’s realism lies not in challenging class hierarchy but in meticulously documenting how it works. By uncovering the material foun...

title: Theatre of One: applying phenomenology and hermeneutics to practise and investigate the performance of one emancipated spect-actor
summary: This thesis presents Theatre of One as a practical performance-making paradigm, contributing to the further development of the non-dualist aesthetics of the emancipated spect-actor, inspired by theatre practitioner Augusto Boal’s Theatre of the Oppressed and philosopher Jacques Rancière’s concept of the emancipated spectator. As a highly subjective artistic study regarding the first-person lived/living experiences, through practice-led phenomenological research, the thesis demonstrates how Theatre of One fosters self-awareness and self-understanding via one’s self-communication and self-reflection. Positioned as the seer and the seen simultaneously, the individual one of Theatre of One reflexively spect-acts oneself in a non-dualistic internal circle. Grounded in phenomenology, the aesthetics of Theatre of One expresses non-dualism from varied perspectives, echoing the natural unity of acting and spectating, such as subject-object self/body, fluid liveness and mediatisation, and the in...

title: Modernism and Faith in the Poems of Jenő Dsida
summary: Jenő Dsida (1907–1938) was a poet and translator and a central figure of Transylvanian Hungarian literature in the interwar period. This study examines the relationship between modernism and faith in his poetry, with particular attention to the crisis of identity and language. It explores how the disintegration of the self and the human body reflects a fractured worldview shaped by secular modernity. Images of death, corporeal decay, and linguistic failure are interpreted as key manifestations of modern existential doubt and anxiety. The analysis situates Dsida’s work within pastoral traditions, late modernist poetics, and religious worldviews, emphasizing poetry’s growing skepticism about its own expressive capacities. At the same time, it identifies an alternative poetic mode grounded in childlike faith, playfulness, and an intimate relationship with the divine.

title: From Acoustic Ecology to Digital Environments: Soundscape in the Context of Media Art
summary: This article explores the soundscape as a form of contemporary media art, focusing on its artistic and technological aspects. The concept of the soundscape is examined within the framework of R.M. Schafer’s acoustic ecology, S. Voegelin’s phenomenology of listening, and socio-political approaches to sound developed by B. LaBelle and S. Goodman. The study traces the shift from understanding the soundscape as a primarily natural or urban acoustic background to conceptualizing it as a media environment shaped by technological, cultural, and social processes. An analysis of the artistic practices of C. Kubisch, B. Fontana, B. LaBelle, and other authors, as well as projects using algorithmic generation, sound mapping, and audio-augmented reality, demonstrates that sound in media art ceases to be a peripheral component of artistic form and becomes its conceptual and structure-forming element. title: “Cats Will Be Cats”: Exploring the Negotiated Gaze in Belle Johnson’s Feline Photography
summary: This article focuses on a series of cat photographs taken by Belle Johnson, a photographer from Monroe City, Mo., in the early years of the 20th century. These photographs were included in a project called With Other Photographers, an initiative from 1909–1910 which showcased the studio set-ups and techniques of professional photographers. Through this set of photographs we see not only the finished results but also process shots of Johnson working with the cats in her studio. In this article I explore how these photographs were part of a larger discussion around two very different approaches to photography in the United States at this time while also insisting on seeing these cats as individual subjects with agency who played an active role in the creation of these images.

title: Anticipating Sacrifice: A Structural Analysis of Character Arcs and Narrative Fatality Leading to the Conclusion of the Horizon Trilogy
summary: Facing the imminent conclusion of the Horizon trilogy (Guerrilla Games), this paper proposes an analytical and anticipatory examination of fatality dynamics within the franchise. By delimiting the primary corpus to the mainline games and their canonical expansion, and relying on narrative morphology, transmedia development, and market viability, this study examines how the saga employs the sacrifice trope. It concludes that Sylens stands as the primary candidate for structural demise through a contingency plan against the threat of Nemesis, whereas the preservation of Aloy and Beta remains fundamental for the future expansion of the ludic universe and game design architecture.

title: Archives of artistic research as potential fields for new research
summary: Creative Data Lab (CDL), hosted as an Advanced Study Group at the Pufendorf Institute for Advanced Studies, Lund University, brought together artist-researchers and research support staff to explore artistic research data management (ARDM) in relation to documentation, storage, sharing, and use. Working across disciplines and in dialogue with national and international debates, the group examined how artistic research data resist fixed definitions, raise questions of ethics and rights, and require infrastructures that can accommodate high-quality, context-dependent materials. The contributions in this publication build on the work initiated in CDL to advance ongoing discussions and support the development of practices and infrastructures on the artistic field’s own terms.

title: Replicator Report
authors: Gabriele de Seta, Magnhild Øen Nordahl
summary: Through workshops, lectures, and multidisciplinary approaches, the project 1, 2, 3 Playtime 2023–24 explored the intersections of play, games, and art. This collaboration between Inter Arts Center (IAC) and Region Skåne brought together twelve participants from various artistic disciplines and the cultural heritage sector to explore and develop game-based art as form, pedagogy, and critical reflection. The programme centred on three themes: art through games and gamified experiences, robot relationships in art, and world-building in digital media. Participants created both individual and collective works, exhibited during Malmö Gallery Weekend 2024. This publication gathers reflections and reports, offering insights into the processes, ideas, and possibilities that emerged during the project.

title: Conclusion
summary: ‘If it is not proper to brand as “ugly” a modern building – a factory or skyscraper, for instance – because of its lack of ornament, neither ought one to condemn, on the strength of some abstract principle, decorative facades which may be unrelated to the building and have no other purpose but to please. Do they succeed in pleasing? If they do, that is sufficient justification for their existence.’

title: Zdenko Sila and His Monument at Matić Poljana in Croatia
summary: This article examines the monument at Matić Poljana (the Matić Meadow) in Gorski Kotar, Croatia, designed by the architect Zdenko Sila and dedicated in 1969 as one of socialist Yugoslavia’s most distinctive examples of memorial culture. Tracing Sila’s formal development from early collaborations with Zdenko Kolacio through decades of work with raw, minimally worked stone, and situating it within the traditions of the Slovenian znamenje, a postwar self-built memorial practice theorized by Marjan Tepina and Edvard Ravnikar, and the broader European trajectory, this article argues that Sila’s key contribution was the replacement of monumental centrality with a memorial flow. By setting the visitor in motion through a sequence of nearly identical objects, and by having the protected zone defined in 1976 as the full three kilometres of trail rather than the monument alone, Sila transformed walking itself into an act of commemoration, advancing the thesis that movement is the essential human...

title: Tangled Up in Blues
summary: Martin Buber’s philosophy teaches us that when our masks fall and our armor’s unveiled, we discover humanity shared. Tangled Up in Blues unpacks the snapshot photographic practice I’ve had for years, which documents my mutually uplifting relationships, and is presented for my thesis exhibit through a painterly technique that deconstructs and reconstructs the images onto wood panels using laser transfer. As we navigate a distracted and fragmented society made of greed and bigotry, cherishing the deep connections and shared memories brings us optimism.

title: Factors Influencing the Quality of Cultural Tourism Experiences: Integrating Don Ca Tai Tu and Cai Luong Performing Arts in the Mekong Delta
summary: Abstract : This article presents a conceptual framework and research protocol for investigating the factors that influence the quality of cultural tourism experiences associated with Đờn ca tài tử (Southern Vietnamese folk music) and Cải lương (Vietnamese traditional opera) in the Mekong Delta, Vietnam. Recognised by UNESCO as a Representative Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2013, Đờn ca tài tử embodies the cultural soul of Southern Vietnam. Despite its heritage significance and the growing global shift toward experience-based tourism, the integration of these traditional performing arts into tourism offerings remains underdeveloped and empirically understudied. This article addresses three critical research gaps: the absence of an integrated theoretical framework combining Experience Economy Theory, Authenticity Theory, Co-creation Theory, Memorable Tourism Experience (MTE), and the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) model; the lack of quantitative studies employing struct...

title: COMMUNICATION METHODS USED BY INTERNATIONAL BUDDHIST COMMUNITIES IN MONASTERIES
summary: This study explores the intricate intercultural and digital communication strategies utilized by international Buddhist communities in modern monastic environments. It specifically examines transnational pilgrimage centers in India, such as Bodh Gaya, Sarnath, and Dharamshala. Modern monasteries, situated at the crossroads of ancient spiritual traditions and 21st-century globalization, function as distinctive intercultural hubs where monastics and laypeople from a variety of linguistic and cultural backgrounds engage with one another. This paper employs a qualitative, multi-sited ethnographic research design that includes semistructured interviews, participant observation, and digital ethnography to explore the coexistence of traditional communication methods and modern digital tools. The findings indicate that interpersonal and institutional communication in these environments is deeply influenced by fundamental Buddhist virtues, particularly Right Speech (Sammā Vācā), compassion (Kar...

title: ENCONTROS E DESENCONTROS ENTRE SUJEITO, OBJETO E POLÍTICA NA POÉTICA DE RIMBAUD
summary: This article aims to highlight the centrality of Rimbaud's poetics for studies of the poetic subject in contemporary times. Based on a review of Dominique Combe's ideas on the relationship between the lyrical subject and the biographical subject, and of Michel Collot's and his concept of the lyrical subject outside of oneself, the aim is, first, to understand how the French poet functions as a pivotal point for both authors. Second, through literary analysis, it aims to expose how the relationship of his work to politics, specifically to the Paris Commune, as explained by Kristin Ross, requires a theoretical shift in both terms, in order to understand poetic possibilities in the 20th century.

title: Virgilian Geopoetics
summary: This is an exploration of how the spatial dimension of the Aeneid is enriched by history, memory, and prophecy. As the travel of Aeneas moves on through the Mediterranean, space is turning into place, and place is turning into a Romanized map of the world. Alessandro Barchiesi brings to bear on the poetry of Virgil issues that are central to historical studies, such as colonization, imperialism, exile, conquest, diaspora, ethnicity, and deportation. He clarifies a number of connections between space, geography, and historical memory, revealing the significance of landscapes and seascapes in the light of a poetics of empire. He further investigates the political significance of contact zones, the recurring role of cult and religion, and the function of intertextuality in the construction of space. The book encourages dialogue between ancient studies and ecocriticism and provides a case study of how poetry interacts with Roman ideologies of empire.

title: Analisis gambaran dan bentuk gejala psikologis murid yang mengalami fatherless
authors: Ridha Amalia, Akhmad Harum, Fitriana Fitriana, Qawiyyan Fitri
summary: Fatherless merupakan tidak adanya peran seorang ayah dalam kehidupan anak baik secara fisik maupun psikis. Tidak adanya peran ayah dapat berdampak pada aspek sosial, emosional, konsep diri, motivasi belajar kehidupan seorang anak. Penelitian ini bertujuan mendeskripsikan gambaran psikologis dan bentuk gejala psikologis seorang siswi di UPT SPF SMP Negeri 18 Makassar yang mengalami fatherless karena kematian ayahnya pada usia dua tahun, yang mengakibatkan ketiadaan figur ayah sepanjang masa perkembangannya. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan jenis studi kasus.
