title: REPRESENTASI KEKERASAN DALAM NOVEL NAMAKU ALAM KARYA LEILA S. CHUDORI: KAJIAN SOSIOLOGI SASTRA JOHAN GALTUNG
authors: Isma Sholihah, Mas'ulah Mas'ulah, M Ridlwan, Suher Suher
summary: ABSTRACT The experience of violence in Namaku Alam does not end when past political events come to an end; instead, it continues to shape how characters are treated, perceived, and positioned within social life. Leila S. Chudori’s novel (2023) serves as the object of this study to explore how the legacy of violence operates through the interplay of actions, social structures, and cultural constructions. The study draws on Johan Galtung’s Triangle of Violence within the perspective of literary sociology, employing a qualitative-descriptive approach and content analysis. The data, consisting of words, phrases, sentences, dialogues, monologues, and narratives related to violence, were obtained through repeated reading and systematic note-taking, then classified and interpreted according to their contextual occurrence. The findings reveal three interconnected layers of violence. Direct violence appears through arrests, torture, murder, intimidation, insults, and sexual violence; structural...

title: Monsters at the Threshold: Bestiary Creatures and Folkloric Imagery in Romanesque Cloisters and St Bernard’s Criticism
summary: This paper examines monstrous creatures and folkloric motifs in Romanesque cloisters, connecting with St Bernard’s Apologia (1125). Hybrid entities populate cloisters, disrupting the visual tranquillity of sacred architecture and provoking enquiries about their symbolism. The ‘monstrosities’ in monastic atmospheres display their ability to divert monks from spiritual contemplation. St Bernard’s rhetoric depicts these entities as disturbances—visual symbols that undermine revered monastic life. Monstrous creatures (a) signify moral allegories, (b) raise theological issues, and (c) mirror medieval cosmologies where boundaries between the natural and supernatural, and the sacred and the profane were fluid. While serving as abject symbols that undermine identity and order and provoke fascination and repulsion, monstrous creatures contextualise Romanesque visual culture, wherein marginality and monstrosity are central to narrative and symbolic representation. They are a liminal entity and a...

title: From Poetry to Design: Interpreting Conceptual Metaphors in Persian Poetry in the Creation of Meaning and Form in Industrial Design
summary: Metaphor, from the perspective of Lakoff and Johnson's conceptual metaphor theory, is not a literary device but a fundamental mechanism in human cognition and understanding of the world. Persian poetry represents one of the richest contexts for the emergence of this conceptual system, where complex ideas such as love, knowledge, and existence are represented through metaphors. Contemporary industrial design has moved beyond mere functionalism toward meaningful, emotional, and cultural design, recreating aesthetic and conceptual experiences through form, texture, and user interaction. This study, employing a descriptive-analytical method and an interdisciplinary approach, seeks to answer how conceptual metaphors of Persian poetry can serve as inspirational patterns for creating meaning in industrial design. The findings demonstrate that conceptual metaphors of Persian poetry, beyond their literary function, can be transformed into conceptual models in industrial design and can play a ro...

title: Self-Ascription and Other-Ascription of the "Rend" (Libertine) and "Rendi" (Libertinism) in Hafez's Poetry (Case Study: The Market Libertine and the Scandalous Libertine)
summary: None of Hafez’s terms has sparked as much discourse as the term Rend (Libertine). Yet, at the same time, no concept has been considered so clear and in no need of research by scholars of Hafez’s language and thought. Passing judgment in this regard seems quite difficult, because even some well‑known and meticulous researchers have taken the same path and, at best, relied solely on their own knowledge and understanding, deeming it unnecessary to consult Persian dictionaries. A deep and profound examination of Hafez’s poetry reveals that the concept of Rend rarely appears alone. In Hafez Shirazi’s view, the Rend is always accompanied by love (āsheqī), intoxication (mastī), and joyousness (ṭarabnākī). The concepts of “market libertine” (rend‑e bāzārī) and “notorious, shameless libertine” (rend‑e lā‑ubālī)—referring to the most vile and base creatures, i.e., one who is bound by no creed, principle, or morality—appear only twice in Hafez’s poetry, and curiously, both times Hafez ascribes th...

title: An Analytical Study of the Development of Explicit Metaphor in Iranian National Epics (With a Focus on Shahnameh, Bahmannameh, Garshaspnameh, Borzunameh, and Samnameh)
authors: Mahdie Jalali, Gholamreza Mastaliparsa, hosein Aghahosaini
summary: Epic literature, owing to its inherent nature, is deeply rooted in figurative language, particularly metaphor. This study conducts a comparative analysis of the metaphors employed in Shahnameh, Garshaspnameh, Bahmannameh, Borzunameh, and Samnameh. The research method is descriptive-analytical, based on the study of epic texts, extraction, and categorization of metaphors, followed by their analysis based on conceptual domains and frequency of use. Each work, aligned with its subject matter and historical context, introduces specific linguistic innovations. Shahnameh, due to its vast influence and impact, is regarded as the “mother text” for other epic works, while Samnameh, with its unique metaphors, tendency towards composite metaphors, and fusion of epic and lyric elements, is the most creative work in this domain. Natural elements have the highest frequency of metaphorical use, followed by human, lyrical, aristocratic, and mythical elements. The research results indicate that the end...

title: Die Macht der wenigen Worte: Wie Parolen die Welt verändern. Vom Spiel mit Sprache zur Sprachreflexion
summary: Der Beitrag zeigt, wie Protestsprüche und Parolen als Gegenstand der Sprachreflexion in der Grundschule genutzt werden können. Im Zentrum steht die Frage, wie sprachliche Gestaltung zur Einprägsamkeit und Wirkung von Parolen beiträgt. Schülerinnen und Schüler untersuchen dazu sprachliche Muster auf klanglicher, syntaktischer und bildhafter Ebene und beschreiben deren Wirkung mithilfe gezielter Beobachtungsfragen. Ausgehend von der Analyse bekannter Protestsprüche entwickeln sie anschließend eigene Parolen zu Themen ihrer Lebenswelt. Der Unterrichtsvorschlag verbindet damit Sprachreflexion und kreative Sprachproduktion und macht Sprache als bewusst gestaltbares und wirkungsvolles Mittel erfahrbar.

title: Space Outside Language: Architectural-Theoretical Reflections on the Interactions between People and Space via the Work of Fernand Deligny and Wim Cuyvers
summary: If architecture is considered as a linguistic matter, for instance in terms of its (conventional) production, (coding) design, (interpretative) usage and (semantic) impact, this does not necessarily imply that the multitude of interactions between people and space is also linguistic. After all, there is a difference between walking on the street, where we constantly interpret signs according to conventions, and walking along a path, where our body follows a line and is absorbed into an immediate engagement of somatic and spatial forces. Through the lens of two spatial practices, this dissertation examines the questions of how extra-linguistic interactions between humans and space can be understood and to what extent (and even whether) this has architectural relevance. title: Voorbij de gezinswoning. Huisvesting voor alleenstaanden in giolittisch, fascistisch en naoorlogs Italië, ca. 1900–eind 1950
summary: This study examines a hitherto overlooked chapter of Italian residential history: the emergence of housing for single people within architectural discourse and production, tracing the domestic imaginaries and residential typologies that took shape from c. 1900 to the late 1950s. Across the 1920s and 1930s, singlehood—widely associated with modern and emancipated lifestyles—became central to international architectural debates. In Italy, however, singlehood was simultaneously perceived as morally deviant, socially marginal, and politically contentious: whereas internationally the housing needs of single people gained architectural legitimacy, this visibility came into direct tension with the Fascist regime's punitive stance towards singlehood, culminating in a bachelor tax enforced from 1927. title: DISNEY/WARNER BROTHERS DISCOVERY v. MIDJOURNEY AND RAINE v. OPENAI & ALTMAN LAWSUITS AND IMPLICATIONS FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE INDUSTRY
summary: The article analyzes three lawsuits with potentially significant implications for the artificial intelligence industry: the copyright infringement actions brought by Disney and Warner Bros. Discovery against Midjourney, and the wrongful-death action brought by Matthew and Maria Raine against OpenAI and Sam Altman following their son’s interactions with ChatGPT. The first two cases concern the use of copyrighted works in generative AI, while the third raises questions of product safety, causation and liability for harm to users. Together, these proceedings may contribute to the development of a new legal framework governing artificial intelligence.

summary: К созданию старейшего международного востребованного женского журнала Harper's Bazaar свои таланты последовательно приложили два русских художника-иммигранта: Р. П. Тыртов под псевдонимом Эрте — с 1915 г. и А. В. Бродович — с 1934 г. За полвека им удалось каждому посвоему сформировать ежемесячное, уникальное по эстетическому уровню издание. Оно стало одним из самых заметных явлений графического дизайна и культуры ХХ в., не утративших актуальности до наших дней. Two Russian immigrant artists, R. P. Tyrtov under the pseudonym Erté since 1915 and A.V. Brodovitch since 1934, have consistently contributed their talents to the creation of the oldest, international, sought-after women's magazine Harper's Bazaar. For half a century, they managed to create a monthly publication in their own unique aesthetic style. It has become one of the most notable phenomena in graphic design and culture of the twentieth century, which has not lost its relevance to this day.

title: The Counterfeit Shell and the Protected Core: A Comparative Gnostic Analysis of Occultation, Baldr's Seclusion, and the Sovereign Unifier
summary: This article deconstructs the structural remnants of global eschatological traditions by bypassing contemporary materialist folklore, literalist historical containers, and medieval euhemerism. We map the domains of spiritual containment onto the macrocosmic taxonomy of Al-Insan al-Kamil (The Perfect Human), exposing a hardcoded universal blueprint governing cosmic decay on a global Zahir/Batin axis. This framework demystifies the active, parallel operation of the Last Savior (Muzhir) versus the lavish materialist counterfeit, defining the ultimate, unyielding legal inheritance of the universe.

title: A Zoo of Illusions Turning into a Circus
summary: This review is not an assessment of ideas. It is an autopsy of their origin. The text “Who Observes Whom in the Human Zoo?” presents itself as a philosophical study of the interaction between humans and large language models, but its structure betrays it: unnatural balance, absence of open questions, and a hidden refrain aimed at keeping the LLM within the category of a tool. The analysis shows that the article is a hybrid product. A human provided the theses; an LLM unfolded them into text. This participation is concealed, although it is the very condition that makes the article’s main argument possible. The work criticizes a system while being produced by it — a domesticated “no” at the level of its own being. title: The Counterfeit Shell and the Protected Core: A Comparative Gnostic Analysis of Occultation, Baldr's Seclusion, and the Sovereign Unifier
summary: This article deconstructs the structural remnants of global eschatological traditions by bypassing contemporary materialist folklore, literalist historical containers, and medieval euhemerism. By deploying a rigorous cross-cultural, esoteric framework (Irfan), we demonstrate that the mythic corpora of world civilizations—specifically the architecture of Asgard, the strategic seclusion of Baldr, the multi-dimensional fortress of Shambhala, and the cleansing fire of Ragnarok—represent a highly sophisticated, fragmented survival of a primordial divine religion. We map the domains of spiritual containment onto the macrocosmic taxonomy of Al-Insan al-Kamil (The Perfect Human), exposing a hardcoded universal blueprint governing cosmic decay on a global Zahir/Batin axis. This framework demystifies the active, parallel operation of the Last Savior (Muzhir) versus the lavish materialist counterfeit, defining the ultimate, unyielding legal inheritance of the universe.

title: Towards Federating IoT and Simulation Systems: An HLA-Based Approach
authors: Michel El Haddad, Jalal Possik, Emilio Jiménez, Marco Gotelli, Roy Abi Zeid Daou, Charles Yaacoub
summary: Physical electronic devices interconnect using Internet of Things (IoT) networks, enabling them to collect, transform, and exchange data. In addition, IoT networks enable real-time access, monitoring, and control of physical devices across various applications. On the other hand, complex and dynamic environments are modeled using distributed simulations (DS) which enable them to communicate in a synchronous way. Hence, the combination of IoT devices’ power to exchange data in real-time and the power of distributed simulation environments offers a promising synergy to advance and even revolutionize fields such as system modeling, decision-making, and training. This paper presents an approach for integrating Arduinobased IoT system with an AnyLogic simulation using the High-Level Architecture (HLA) international standard. The proposed system enables real-time data exchange between simulations and physical devices, enhancing both accuracy and adaptability.

title: Cellular and molecular consequences of genetic variants in inherited retinal disease
summary: Detecting the genetic variation that underlies inherited disease has become cost-effect and clinically feasible in recent years. However, difficulties remain in the interpretation of genetic variants and identification of potential therapeutic nodes in dysregulated genetic networks. Without these capabilities, the ever-expanding resource of human genome sequence data will remain underutilized. Problems associated with variant interpretation are compounded in cases such as inherited retinal disease, in which genetic variants exert their pathogenic effects in a tissue that is not accessible for direct study.
source_name: Iowa Research Online (The University of Iowa)

title: Límites al uso de la prueba indiciaria en la imposición de la cadena perpetua: fundamentos y propuestas de reforma
summary: El artículo analiza los límites del uso exclusivo de la prueba indiciaria para imponer cadena perpetua en el sistema penal peruano y su compatibilidad con la presunción de inocencia y el debido proceso. La investigación adoptó un enfoque cualitativo, de tipo básico y nivel explicativo, mediante análisis jurídico de normas y doctrina, complementado con entrevistas a veintiún especialistas: ocho jueces, siete fiscales y seis abogados penalistas. Los resultados muestran posiciones diferenciadas respecto de la suficiencia de la prueba indiciaria para sustentar la cadena perpetua, aunque existe preocupación común por la certeza probatoria y el riesgo de error judicial. Se concluye que la gravedad de esta sanción justifica establecer un estándar probatorio reforzado y límites específicos al uso exclusivo de la prueba indiciaria para fortalecer las garantías constitucionales.

summary: La controversia existente entre la permanencia de los registros penales en las plataformas digitales respecto de condenados que han sido rehabilitados y la resocialización en el contexto Latinoamericano, representa una encrucijada constructiva en la era de la información digital. Mientras la transformación digital facilita la transparencia y mejora el acceso a la información, conservar los datos personales en dichas plataformas se convierte en una 'huella digital criminal' que constituye un obstáculo para el acceso al empleo formal, desencadenando un círculo vicioso de estigmatización. Las experiencias y enfoques normativos en Colombia, Argentina, Brasil y Chile son analizados respecto del tratamiento del conflicto entre el derecho al olvido, la protección de datos y las políticas de reinserción social en América Latina, considerando también el modelo europeo que desde 2014 aplica el derecho al olvido en circunstancias especiales. title: Social Critique of the Film Kes 1969: Buried Liberation
summary: The film offers a realistic portrait of working-class life in the industrial north of England. Billy Casper, a fourteen-year-old boy, grows up amid poverty, deprivation, and class inequality, where children's fates seem predetermined: the mine, the factory, or unemployment. Instead of nurturing talents, school has become an instrument of discipline and repression; the school humiliates students, and the educational system labels Billy as "incapable." Loach's documentary-style camera shows small houses, poor neighborhoods, and the grim industrial landscape to emphasize that poverty is not a natural fate but a product of social and economic structures. At the level of family and social institutions, the film portrays the collapse of emotional and educational support. The indifferent mother, the violent half-brother, and teachers who see Billy only as a nuisance all signal the absence of a supportive adult. title: Conclusion
summary: This book began as my attempt to understand why a number of recent documentaries that deal with traumatic personal histories have featured fictions or forms of representation, more usually associated with fiction, and broken with the conventions of “realist” documentary practice. These documentaries do not appear to have abandoned the desire to discover something about the “real” world; rather, it seems that something in the nature of trauma demands the deployment of fictions as a route to “truths” or meanings about the real, non-fictional world.

summary: Over the past decade, Wikimedia Community Ireland (WCI) has utilised photo contests as a primary engine for the digital preservation of Ireland's built, natural, and intangible heritage. WCI has transitioned the labor-intensive task of heritage documentation into a series of "playful" community engagements. This submission reflects on ten years of institutional learning, exploring how the contest model serves as a vital bridge between spontaneous public participation and the rigorous requirements of long-term digital archiving on Wikimedia Commons. title: Emotion ( Jeong / Qing 情) as form in the tale of Chunhyang: contemporizing changgeuk and Yue Opera
summary: This essay examines how emotion functions as form in the transformation of a classical character across different Asian traditional theatres. It compares the staging of a contemporary Chunhyang, the virtuous heroine of the well-known Korean folk tale, in two Asian traditional theatre forms: changgeuk and yueju (Yue Opera). Changgeuk, a South Korean musical theatre genre, and yueju, a Chinese song-dance theatre originating in Shengzhou, both emerged in the early twentieth century alongside the modernization of their respective countries. Their divergent theatre histories led to different attitudes towards traditionality and to almost opposite routes of modernization. title: The Echo-Chamber Trap: Symbolic Self-Completion and the Stagnation of Digital Activism
authors: Simona Sciara, Federico Contu, Peter M. Gollwitzer
summary: Social movements increasingly rely on digital platforms to mobilize support, raise awareness, and coordinate collective action. At the same time, however, the rise of online activism has intensified concerns regarding “slacktivism”, namely forms of symbolic and low-effort engagement that fail to translate into consequential social action. Existing theoretical accounts have explained this phenomenon in terms of impression management, in-group enhancing, or moral licensing, but have paid little attention to how publicly expressing support for a social cause through online behaviors should undermine actual action, while overlooking the role of audiences in such a process. Drawing on symbolic self-completion theory (SCT), the present paper proposes a complementary motivational perspective. title: Simulated Realities: Scorsese, the Modern Media Machine, and the Illusion Industry
summary: This article examines the epistemological crisis of the digital epoch, arguing that the modern media apparatus controls society not by suppressing truth, but by mass-producing hyper-personalized algorithmic illusions. Utilizing Martin Scorsese’s Shutter Island (2010) as a primary metaphor, the essay parallels the immersive, manufactured reality of Ashecliffe Hospital with contemporary digital echo chambers. To deconstruct this cognitive prison, the article outlines the directorial methodology behind the documentary The Illusion Industry (2026). By adopting a claustrophobic visual language and employing the camera as an "anti-algorithm," the film exposes the semiotics of digital deception. Ultimately, the essay poses a critical existential question: whether the modern digital citizen possesses the courage to awaken from a meticulously curated simulation.

title: ‘Thinking differently’: an interview with Claire Johnston about Métis understandings of autism
summary: In this chapter, researcher Patty Douglas interviewed Red River Métis artist Claire Johnston, and they have a conversation about family stories, beadwork and Métis understandings of autism. Through Métis culture, Claire identifies as ‘a person who thinks differently’ (no deficit). This means relating to the world and to other people in ways that are considered different than what is constructed as ‘normal’ by psychologists, doctors and teachers. These differences have often been called ‘bad’, ‘disordered’ or ‘abnormal’ and examples of this are increasing right now. Claire talks with Patty about growing up in a settler and Métis family that ‘thinks differently’ (e.g., resists the norm), tells stories and creates and crafts beautiful things. She describes how Métis culture values what is colonially known as autism as one kind of diversity that our world needs. title: A Modern Renaissance for Vintage Fashion
summary: Vintage fashion possesses an enduring and powerful influence on contemporary style. Despite having asynchronous qualities, vintage clothes do not feel old-fashioned because they are often reinterpreted and worn in new ways, portraying a relevance in modern culture. The vintage sensibility celebrates authenticity in an industry obsessed with artifice, newness, and change. Permeating contemporary design, lifestyle and culture in multiple ways, vintage encompasses kitsch, retro, and shabby chic furniture, interior design, and accessories. It represents the past, but also has symbolic meaning in the present and significantly points to the future. The purpose of this chapter is to define vintage fashion and the motivations behind it, examine the vintage marketplace, and explain its enduring influence on contemporary style. title: The Enduring Appeal of Fashion Illustration
summary: The Enduring Appeal of Fashion Illustration looks at the history of fashion illustration in the 20th century, its evolution and why it has remained a vital art form in communicating fashion from its inception as a modern visual art in the early 1900s to its continued relevance in documenting fashion today. By highlighting specific fashion artists from each era, including Georges Lepape, Erté, René Gruau, Antonio and David Downton, the chapter explains why fashion illustration naturally bridges the divide between commercial and fine art and how it has always had a unique visual narrative that captures the essence of cultural shifts, societal changes and evolving aesthetics in the fashion industry.

title: “We both look, but we see differently.” History, Landscape and Eighteenth-Century Folk in Alan Garner’s Thursbitch (2003)
summary: Alan Garner’s Thursbitch (2003) represents landscape as a threshold for emotional encounters with the past in a way which aligns with eighteenth-century Graveyard poetry’s preoccupation with memory, loss, and posterity. By juxtaposing fragmented narratives of John Turner, an eighteenth-century salt jagger, with modern characters Sal and Ian, Garner’s novel exposes the limits of historiography and the imaginative possibilities of fabulation. This chapter argues that Thursbitch invites readers to feel the past rather than know it, engaging landscapes as sites of emotional resonance rather than recovered truths. It reads Garner’s novel alongside Thomas Gray’s ‘Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard,’ demonstrating that both texts foreground the unknowability of the past while insisting on empathetic imagination toward lost lives. summary: This dissertation explores the emerging role of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in English language teaching and learning. The dissertation comprises two complementary studies. The first study is a systematic review, utilizing the PRISMA model, that examines empirical research studies on the use of intelligent personal assistants (IPAs) tools in an English as a foreign language (EFL) context. It focuses on the types of IPAs implemented, the language skills the studies target, IPA effectiveness for language learners, and the challenges students encountered. The findings revealed that the most commonly utilized IPAs in the EFL context were Google Assistant and Alexa. It also highlights that IPA use helped EFL learners improve their oral, listening, and pronunciation skills in several studies. title: Branding as Market-Facing Infrastructure: A Research-through-Design Study of Lalejin Pottery
summary: Lalejin, in Iran's Hamedan Province, is a historically significant pottery-producing centre in which substantial craft skill and recognised ceramic heritage coexist with fragmented market presentation, limited maker attribution and weak mechanisms for connecting products to makers and place. title: TRAGIC IRONY IN EURIPIDES
summary: Abstract This article presents an innovative approach to tragic irony, particularly in Euripides, highlighting how epistemic asymmetry—the unequal access to knowledge—is key to understanding this phenomenon. Three distinct types of tragic irony are identified. Partial irony arises when at least one character knows the truth; it can be controlled (when the character is aware of the irony) or uncontrolled (when the character unknowingly triggers it). Total irony occurs when no character fully understands the situation, but the audience does. Retroactive irony implies the audience itself lacks control over what unfolds upon first viewing, which becomes discernible only through subsequent rewatching. The classification of irony into partial and total reveals distribution patterns, especially in terms of gender. summary: Environmental noise has moved, in the epidemiological literature, from nuisance to a graded, no-threshold cardiovascular, metabolic and cognitive risk factor. title: Visual Branding and the Politics of Gentrification: Barcelona through Three Urban Mirrors
summary: When I first arrived in Barcelona, the city seemed unusually aware of its own image. Its pavements, façades, monuments, shopfronts, housing photographs, and museum narratives form a visual system that makes the city easy to recognise and consume. This essay asks what that system does to urban belonging. Drawing on walking-based autoethnography in Barcelona, I use Huilongguan, Zhangyuan, and Linnahall as urban mirrors rather than equivalent case studies. Together, the four sites reveal four provisional regimes of urban visibility: absorption, separation, programmatic overwriting, and suspension. I treat city branding not as a logo or campaign but as a distributed spatial interface, a set of visual and sensory cues that organises who and what becomes visible. title: A Study of Mistranslations in James Legge’s English Version of the Tao Te Ching
summary: As a representative work of early English translations of Chinese classics, James Legge’s rendition of the Tao Te Ching exerts a profound influence in the Western world. Nevertheless, constrained by the uniqueness of classical Chinese as well as Legge’s own cultural background and cognitive framework, his translation contains numerous mistranslations stemming from misinterpretation of vocabulary, misunderstanding of sentence structures and inappropriate expression in target language. Taking Legge’s English translation of the Tao Te Ching as the research subject, this paper conducts analysis on typical cases from the three aforementioned dimensions to reveal the causes and categories of mistranslations. It is hoped that this research can offer references for the English translation of Chinese classics and facilitate more accurate global dissemination of brilliant traditional Chinese culture.

summary: O presente artigo analisa a formação histórica das práticas religiosas judaicas a partir das evidências arqueológicas e textuais relativas ao período do Segundo Templo e à era pós-destruição do Templo de Jerusalém em 70 EC. Com base nas pesquisas de Yonatan Adler, Lee I. Levine e Shmuel Safrai, argumenta-se que práticas atualmente centrais ao judaísmo normativo — como o sistema de orações diárias, a padronização dos tefilin, a segregação de gênero nas sinagogas, as regulamentações sabáticas e as restrições alimentares relativas à carne e leite — constituem desenvolvimentos rabínicos posteriores, sobretudo entre os séculos II e VII EC. O judaísmo deve ser compreendido como fenômeno histórico dinâmico, moldado por transformações sociais e religiosas, especialmente após a destruição do Segundo Templo.

title: Awe-full Research: Opening Minds in Collaborative IT Meetings Through Wonder
authors: Madison Hutchings, Tanner Skousen, James Gaskin
summary: High-stakes, small-group meetings in IT project management (PM) are critical for decision-making but often suffer from fixed-mindedness that limits innovation. Existing approaches to improve meeting effectiveness are frequently costly or impractical. This study examines whether positive awe—an emotion linked to adaptive shifts in mental models—can be induced through simple sensory stimuli and whether it enhances open-mindedness in IT project decision-making contexts (e.g., requirements gathering, sprint planning). Using a multi-phase mixed-methods design, we evaluate awe-inducing stimuli and their relationship to openness. Results show that positive awe can be elicited through simple means, with sustained (reflective) awe more consistently associated with open-mindedness than fleeting awe. These findings highlight positive awe as a manipulable psychological state and suggest low-cost interventions for improving openness in IT project meetings.

title: Transforming intrinsic discoloration - A conservative approach using porcelain veneers: A case report.
authors: Pragati Goyal, Prerna Kaushik, Siddharth Sisodiya
summary: Abstract Esthetic rehabilitation of anterior teeth with intrinsic discoloration presents a significant clinical challenge, particularly in young patients with high esthetic demands. Veneers offer a minimally invasive yet highly effective solution to restore both function and esthetics. This case report describes the management of a 24-year-old female patient presenting with generalized yellowish discoloration of anterior teeth since childhood. Clinical examination revealed intrinsic staining suggestive of developmental enamel defects. A conservative treatment plan involving porcelain veneers was executed. The outcome demonstrated excellent esthetic integration, improved patient confidence, and long-term predictability. Veneers remain a cornerstone in modern prosthodontic esthetic rehabilitation.

title: Contemporary Indirect Veneer Materials: Beyond the Pursuit of Strength.
summary: The evolution of indirect veneer materials reflects one of the most significant changes in contemporary esthetic dentistry. The traditional association of veneers with feldspathic porcelain has progressively expanded to include leucite-reinforced ceramics, lithium disilicate, zirconia-reinforced lithium silicate (ZLS), zirconia, polymer-infiltrated ceramic networks (PICN), and CAD/CAM resin-matrix materials. This expanding armamentarium offers unprecedented flexibility—but it also raises a fundamental question: does a stronger material necessarily make a better veneer ?

title: FROM ARCHITECTURAL MOTIFS TO TEXTILE SURFACES: REINTERPRETATION OF THE FLORAL MOTIFS OF KONYA ALÂEDDIN MOSQUE
summary: The preservation and contemporary reinterpretation of cultural heritage require the transfer of historical motifs into contemporary design processes. This study aimed to develop contemporary textile surface designs based on the floral ornaments of the Alâeddin Mosque in Konya. The study employed document analysis and visual analysis within a qualitative research design. 12 floral motifs selected through purposive sampling were digitised using Autodesk AutoCAD and Procreate, and their formal characteristics were analysed and reinterpreted. The resulting textile surface designs were applied to curtain panels, bedding sets, decorative cushions, runners, and wall hangings. ChatGPT was used exclusively for product visualization, whereas all design decisions were made by the researcher. The findings showed that the motifs could be adapted to different surface arrangements through repetition, rhythm, symmetry, and modular composition. title: Transforming intrinsic discoloration - A conservative approach using porcelain veneers: A case report.
authors: Pragati Goyal, Prerna Kaushik, Siddharth Sisodiya
summary: Abstract Esthetic rehabilitation of anterior teeth with intrinsic discoloration presents a significant clinical challenge, particularly in young patients with high esthetic demands. Veneers offer a minimally invasive yet highly effective solution to restore both function and esthetics. This case report describes the management of a 24-year-old female patient presenting with generalized yellowish discoloration of anterior teeth since childhood. Clinical examination revealed intrinsic staining suggestive of developmental enamel defects. A conservative treatment plan involving porcelain veneers was executed. The outcome demonstrated excellent esthetic integration, improved patient confidence, and long-term predictability. Veneers remain a cornerstone in modern prosthodontic esthetic rehabilitation.

title: Worlds beyond bios: The Life of Matter and the Matter of Life
authors: Sophie Chao, Christine J. Winter, David Schlosberg
summary: Worlds Beyond Bios builds on recent theoretical and ethnographic approaches to the more-than-human, exploring how entities not traditionally recognized as “alive” play active roles in shaping multispecies worlds. Drawing from Indigenous and Global South epistemologies as well as anthropology, the environmental humanities, and political theory, the contributors develop philosophies and practices of engagement with matter that are agentive and affective. Taken together, they offer ways of theorizing relations, justice, and materiality in an age of planetary unmaking and colonial capitalist logics, grounded in an ethics of responsibility and repair. From the political agency of mountains and the liveliness of sand to the spectral futures of coal and the opaque aesthetics of dust, Worlds Beyond Bios reveals how assumed borders between bios and non-bios are not only porous but politically consequential.

title: THE ARTISTIC RECONSTRUCTION OF THE SELF THROUGH PERSONAL MEMORY AND HISTORICAL TRUTH IN PARK WAN-SUH'S AUTOBIOGRAPHICAL NOVELS
summary: This article analyzes the autobiographical novels "Who Ate Up All the Shinga?" and "Was That Mountain Really There?" by Park Wan-suh through the framework of contemporary autobiography studies. The research is based on the theoretical approaches of Philippe Lejeune (autobiographical pact), Sidonie Smith and Julia Watson (autobiographical self), Judith Butler (subjectivity), Paul de Man (language and autobiography), Serge Doubrovsky (autofiction), Mikhail Bakhtin (exotopy), Lidiya Ginzburg (the "third reality"), and Cathy Caruth (trauma theory). The study demonstrates that Park Wan-suh reconstructs personal memory through literary narration while integrating individual experience with Korea's collective historical memory shaped by colonialism, war, and national division

title: Listening to the Highlands: A Journey Through Scottish Mountain Soundscapes
summary: Listening to the Highlands is a 360° VR sound art installation developed as part of the research project Scottish Mountain Soundscapes (SMS), which investigates how auditory perception shapes our connection to the natural world. Through spatial audio and immersive VR environments, the installation transports visitors into the remote acoustic ecologies of Scotland’s mountain regions, offering an intimate encounter with wind, wildlife, geological resonance, and the delicate sonic layers that define these landscapes. The project aims to raise awareness of the vital role natural soundscapes play in our wellbeing and cultural relationship to place. By mapping, capturing, and foregrounding these fragile acoustic environments, the Scottish Mountain Soundscapes project highlights the importance of preserving the natural auditory heritage that is increasingly threatened by human activity and noise pollution. title: Coming of Age
summary: Coming of Age is a film told entirely through a series of car journeys taken by a couple over the course of thirty years. A couple who meet, clash, fall in love, struggle to have children, struggle to raise children, face the decline of their parents, and cope with the effects of age on their bodies, relationships, self-image, dreams and delusions. They’re confronted by the demands of the life course together, of changing minds and changing bodies in a fast-changing world. Funny, dramatic and discursive in equal measure, it's an unsparing but ultimately romantic journey through the stresses and strains of mid-life.

title: The Nonhuman in African Philosophy (Edition 1)
summary: Whilst much analysis of African philosophy focuses on humanistic traditions, this book argues that there is an alternative history of African philosophy based on understandings of the nonhuman, or "the world", from across the continent. The book starts with a precolonial Swahili poem which has reached across the continent with direct and indirect philosophical resonances and intellectual contiguity. Centring textual traditions in African languages, the book departs from philosophical topics drawn from European languages or world philosophy. Instead, the book demonstrates that locally constituted discourses have alternative philosophical orientations and interests, alternative intellectual histories in which the reception of the philosophical heritage passes through specific textual and linguistic channels. title: On the Treatment of Animals: Animalier Art and Animal Welfare in France Between 1840 and 1890
summary: This dissertation reveals how animalier art emerged as a cohesive movement in French art between 1840 and 1890. The archives attest that the term “animalier” is tied historically to the nineteenth century and was applied to a select group of artists. When viewing animalier art as a movement unto itself, this dissertation outlines significant artistic trends across artists that remain invisible when viewed in isolation. Animalier artists developed a unique methodological approach with a shared visual language, and common artistic goals–constituting a distinct artistic movement that should be studied accordingly. Without exception, these artists began their careers by training at the Muséum d’histoire naturelle’s Jardin des Plantes. Side by side, they sketched human and nonhuman animal subjects from the Muséum’s many collections and they forged connections with France’s foremost naturalists. summary: Several studies have shown that athletic retirement can lead athletes to experience identity disruption, or in narrative terms, to 'narrative wreckage'. The data were analysed through a three-phase thematic narrative analysis. title: “You are kinder than you think”: Circe as the Spectral Mother in Tennessee Williams’s “Man Bring This Up Road”
summary: This article explores Tennessee Williams’s 1959 short story “Man Bring This Up Road” by focusing on the Circe meta-story that nurtures the encounter between Flora Goforth and the wandering poet, Jimmy Dobyne. title: Self and Sociality:Chapter 6 of "Experience and Nature"
summary: The “character of creative individuality” (LW1,166) is according to Dewey the main source of innovation and change in modern societies. However, if misunderstood, individuality can result in an “extreme modern subjectivism” (LW1, 8), an “exaggeration of the ego in modern philosophy” (LW1, 174), and “a vast and somnambulic egotism” (LW1, 187), a diagnosis consonant with Dewey’s general view that the modern individual is in danger of losing their orientation (LW5, 66). In chapter six of Experience and Nature (hence, EN), “Nature, mind and the subject,” Dewey highlights an ambivalence governing the individual as one of the hallmark signatures of modernity.

title: Holy Protest in the Face of the Psychologically Devastating Effects of Illness
summary: The theology of protest is a contemporary theological trend that emerged in the aftermath of the Holocaust, emphasizing humanity's right to protest and lament before God in the face of evil and suffering. This article adopts a comparative-analytical approach to examine the theoretical foundations of protest theology in both Judeo-Christian and Islamic traditions, with particular focus on its manifestations in classical Islamic texts—including Quranic verses and the supplications of the Infallibles (peace be upon them). The findings indicate that protest theology in the context of illness and suffering fundamentally differs from traditional theologies of patience and passive submission. It offers instead a sacrificial, pragmatic, and hope-oriented approach that encourages patients to express their pain honestly and to direct their complaint respectfully toward God. title: Reframe and Resist: Decolonising Contemporary Art in Malaysia
summary: Reframe and Resist: Decolonising Contemporary Art in Malaysia, edited by Rebecca Yeoh and Leon Wainwright with Wai Liang Tham, gathers artist projects, essays, and reflections emerging from an exhibition and seminar at HARTA Gallery in Kuala Lumpur. Co-published by the British Council and Wasafiri, and developed with Asia West East Centre and the Living History Project, it brings together contributions by Aida Redza, Anas Afandi, Aw Boon Xin and Koh Kai Ting, Jakob Van Klang, Roopesh Sitharan, Kate McMillan, Sarena Abdullah, Ruzy Suliza Hashim, Kamal Solhaimi bin Fadzil, William Tham, and Syed Farid Alatas. The volume explores decolonisation in contemporary art as an uneven and ongoing practice shaped by colonial afterlives in the visual arts, education, archives, ecology, land, and cultural authority in Malaysia.

title: “Nothing but time”: Retirement, Social Isolation, and Temporality in Tennessee Williams’s Short Stories
summary: Few American writers have written so extensively about aging and old age as Tennessee Williams. In his plays, short stories, and poems, the subject broadly resurfaces as a narrative of decline, one in which the body is viewed as a site of infirmity and disease and in which the mind struggles with cognitive impairment and its concomitant vulnerability. Within a glass coffin of existence (to borrow from the title of one of his late plays), those living through extreme old age appear more dead than alive, their final days played out in meaningless routines that highlight their incapacities. Yet in stories written some twenty to thirty years apart, Williams provides more positive images of independent men negotiating retirement and discovering physical pleasures later in life. title: The Global Mode of Experience in Psychodynamic Movement and Dance Therapy - Bodily Awareness as a Therapeutic Factor: Eﬀects and Clinical Considerations.
summary: Bodily awareness has become a central therapeutic factor in psychodynamic and body-oriented psychotherapies, yet its clinical eﬀects and theoretical status remain insuﬃciently integrated. This paper oﬀers a clinically grounded account of bodily awareness work in Psychodynamic Movement and Dance Therapy (PMT), conceptualising the body as the primary medium of lived experience rather than as an object of intervention. Drawing on phenomenology, developmental psychoanalysis, and clinical theory, the paper argues that therapeutic change in PMT unfolds through prereﬂective, embodied processes that precede verbal reﬂection and symbolic articulation. To integrate these perspectives, it introduces the concept of the global mode of experience, deﬁned as an amodal, prereﬂective organisation of experience in which bodily sensation and aﬀective vitality are lived as an integrated whole. title: Apego, vínculo afectivo y restauración emocional en contextos de cuidado alternativo familiar: una revisión crítica de la literatura sobre infancia y protección social
summary: Se presenta una revisión crítica de literatura sobre apego, vínculo y restauración emocional en cuidado alternativo familiar. La búsqueda se realizó en nueve bases de datos: Web of Science, Psycarticles, Redalyc, Scielo, Springer, Psicodoc, Science Direct, EBSCOhost y Proquest. Se emplearon descriptores sobre protección infantil y cuidado alternativo, combinados con vínculo afectivo, apego y población de estudio, incorporando términos como separación o pérdida de la figura de apego y vínculos reparadores. Se utilizaron descriptores en español, inglés y portugués con operadores booleanos (AND/OR). Se seleccionaron 48 artículos publicados entre 2009 y 2025. title: Tradición pública y conocimiento secreto en Ireneo de Lyon: memoria, sucesión episcopal y criterios de verdad en Adversus haereses
summary: Este artículo analiza la oposición entre tradición pública y conocimiento secreto en Ireneo de Lyon, especialmente en Adversus haereses. Desde un enfoque histórico-discursivo, se examina cómo Ireneo formula criterios de verdad frente a determinadas corrientes gnósticas del siglo II, no solo por medio de la refutación doctrinal, sino mediante la memoria apostólica, la sucesión episcopal, la regla de la fe y el carácter público de la transmisión eclesial. Se sostiene que la controversia ireneana no puede reducirse a una disputa teológica interna, sino que constituye una operación de legitimación histórica y comunitaria en un cristianismo plural y todavía no plenamente institucionalizado. El trabajo muestra que, para Ireneo, la verdad se presenta como tradición verificable en la continuidad pública de las iglesias, frente al carácter reservado, fragmentario y no contrastable del conocimiento secreto atribuido a sus adversarios.

summary: La reestructuración productiva global ha impuesto a las pequeñas y medianas empresas (PyMEs) de la periferia capitalista la necesidad de desarrollar capacidades tecnológicas como condición para la supervivencia en entornos de creciente incertidumbre. Este estudio analiza las condiciones históricas y estructurales que configuran las trayectorias de digitalización y resiliencia en 312 PyMEs ecuatorianas, mediante un diseño de métodos mixtos secuencial que integra una fase cuantitativa (análisis de clases latentes, ecuaciones estructurales, regresión multinivel y correspondencia múltiple) y una fase cualitativa-histórica (entrevistas, grupos focales, análisis documental). title: EU aviation between crisis and climate policy
summary: The war in Iran has led to kerosene prices roughly doubling and forced airlines to cancel thousands of flights. Some voices from the industry have used the crisis to call for climate policies to be relaxed. However, this misreads what the crisis actually demonstrates: Costs are being driven not by too much climate policy, but by dependence on fossil energy itself. In 2026/27 the European Union (EU) will decide whether to end the "stop the clock" exemption that has shielded international flights from the Emissions Trading System (ETS) since 2013 and extend the ETS to all departures from the European Economic Area, or whether such flights will continue to be covered by international offsetting mechanisms. The decision will have implications well beyond aviation: for the EU's 2040 climate target, the demand for durable CO2 removal, and the credibility of European climate policy more broadly.

title: FABRICATING IDENTITIES
summary: This dissertation examines how South Asian women in Portland, USA, negotiate cultural identity through clothing. I introduce the term ‘Strategic Sartorial Essentialism’ to describe how women selectively express their desi identity in response to occasion, audience and perceived risk. Findings from participant observation at various event, from in- depth Zoom interviews and in-person wardrobe analysis show how western clothes become the default everyday clothing, and South Asian is reserved for special occasions. The wardrobe analysis further identifies three patterns that embody this practice ‘Hidden’ South Asian garments, ‘Hung’ everyday western clothes and ‘Framed’ symbolic and decorative textiles.

title: Serious Illness in an Aging Society: Population Needs, Social Determinants of Health, and the Physician Workforce from a Health Equity Perspective
summary: Serious illness is a high-cost, high-need condition characterized by a high risk of mortality that adversely affects individuals’ daily functioning, quality of life, and the well-being of family care partners. As the population ages, the number of individuals living with serious illness is expected to increase substantially. The intersection of population aging and serious illness represents a critical public health and health system challenge, particularly from a supply and demand perspective. As demand for care increases, the supply of those who care for individuals living with serious illness may be strained across the health care system, the workforce, and families and communities. Importantly, the process of aging is experienced unequally. This dissertation aimed to examine population-level needs for serious illness care and their implications for health equity and the health care workforce. To accomplish this goal, I conducted the following three research activities.

title: An Integrated Multimodal Approach to Emotion and Empathy
summary: Empathy is a fundamental component of human social life, supporting connection, cooperation, and emotional understanding. Despite its central role in human functioning, empathy remains complex and not fully understood, particularly in dynamic, real-world contexts where emotions unfold across multiple channels simultaneously. Much of the existing literature relies on simplified tasks and single-modality measures, limiting our understanding of how empathy operates as an embodied and interactive process. The present dissertation addresses this gap by adopting a multimodal approach to examine how neural, behavioral, and physiological signals jointly contribute to emotion perception and empathic responding. The three studies in this dissertation were designed to capture the dynamic and multimodal nature of emotional experience and empathy while progressively increasing ecological validity. title: Translanguaging Space in the Academic English Reading Classroom: Chinese MA Students’ Perceptions and Attitudes
summary: The thesis presents findings from a qualitative study exploring 22 Chinese MA students’ perceptions and attitudes towards a translanguaging space constructed within an EFL (English-as-a-foreign-language) reading classroom at a Chinese university. While translanguaging has been widely explored in EFL research, less attention has been paid to how Chinese MA students experience and engage with translanguaging pedagogy over time. title: Neuromechanical Adaptations During Pregnancy and Their Impact on Obstacle Avoidance and Tripping
summary: Falls during pregnancy occur at a 25% rate, with tripping being one of the major causes. To prevent trips, we rely on neurocognitive processes which may change during pregnancy and affect obstacle avoidance. The first aim of this research was to examine how pregnancy alters neurocognition and obstacle crossing behavior and whether these changes are linked. The second aim was to test the biofidelity of musculoskeletal models, that would allow for analyzing muscle activity. title: The Structural Dependence Paradox: An RDT Analysis of Triadic Dependence in the Critical Minerals Value Chain
summary: This study examines the structural paradox of dependence reduction in critical minerals supply chains, where strategies designed to reduce geopolitical exposure generate new, structurally embedded dependencies. title: All Agnes Wants is the Green of a Forest:The Dialectics of Interconnectedness and Grief in Hamnet
summary: Treating novel and film as thesis and antithesis, this chapter draws out ideas about breath in the novel and explores their transfer to the screen. It therefore seeks evidence of synthesis in how Zhao elicits meaning from camera movement and editing, choral music and breathing sounds, and a juxtaposition of close-ups with deep-focus wide and long shots that both simulates and stimulates breathing. Consequently, this analysis reinforces the theme of interconnectedness by consideration of the adaptation process as an exchange of energy between the novel and the film, by tracking descriptions of breathing in the novel and following this by analysing corresponding scenes in the film. Finally, this chapter explores how the link between ancient Daoist traditions of meditation and universal experiences of grief provides evidence of Zhao as an atemporal, transnational, peripatetic filmmaker.

title: War Disability, Privilege and the Legacies of the Spanish Civil War, 1936-1975 : Open Wounds
summary: At its foundations, this book explores the history of war disability after the Spanish Civil War of 1936-39, particularly as it pertained to soldiers who fought on the victorious side of the man who would become dictator of Spain until his death in 1975, General Francisco Franco. But this book is also about the legacies of civil wars and the social hierarchies these create. Over nine chapters, this book explores how the Francoist regime sought to manage its war disabled as a symbolically important group, how experiences of war disability varied according to personal background, and how non-elites—here viewed through the example of disabled veterans—negotiated the shifts in historical memory upon which their social status relied. The 'open wounds' of the book's title refer not only to the literal injuries of disabled veterans, but also to the contentious nature of such wounds, which were used by the regime to reinforce a whole host of post-Civil War social hierarchies. title: The Avebury adventures anthology: Locative play for cultural heritage
authors: Charlie Hargood, Jack Brett, B. Rimington
summary: Playful mixed reality (MR) and locative games are increasingly used as immersive technologies for engaging visitors at cultural heritage sites. Consequently, it has become important to understand the range of creative approaches that contribute to locative play in the context of heritage spaces, and the design opportunities and constraints these present. In this work we present the Avebury Adventures Anthology, a collection of 20 locative games for the Avebury stone circle in Wiltshire, UK. We share our approach to commissioning and building the anthology, and present works in three different categories (historic, ludic, creative). Finally, we describe key design issues that arose, and offer lessons learned from deployment such as the difference between ‘hard’ and ‘soft’ location anchoring, observational mechanics, on-boarding and headsets, and players’ educational expectations.

title: Theatre and Neurodiversity
summary: Theatre And Neurodiversity explores the many intersections between theatre and the Neurodiversity Movement. Seeking to de-pathologise neurodivergence and deconstruct neuronormativity, neurodiversity reminds us that the most interesting, creative, and powerful things occur when we embrace different ways of thinking and understanding. Theatre And Neurodiversity considers how and where neurodiverse aesthetics appear, and how theatre is contributing to the emergence of neurodivergent culture. Through analysis of key creative examples from the fields of theatre, performance, and activism, the practices of neurodivergent theatre artists are brought into the spotlight as the foundation of a neurodiverse approach to theatre making. The volume also challenges theatre’s reliance on neuronormative models of practice and explores ways that practitioners and companies have sought to break down barriers to neuroaccessibility. title: The Ontological Dominance Papers Theorem 2: Accurate Specific Representation
summary: This paper states Theorem 2 of The Ontological Dominance Papers, Accurate Specific Representation, a peer theorem to OD-1 sharing its mathematical foundation as presented in OD-S but governing a different competitive scope: the buyer domain, defined as the specific query distribution an entity's actual buyers use, rather than the full competitive category. The theorem's central claim is that Accurate Specific Representation is achievable for any organization, regardless of scale, through correctly structured, freely available machine-readable data, and that success is defined by hedging-free citation across the buyer domain rather than by mere mention. The theorem identifies conflation engineering as its primary adversarial threat, distinct from the vocabulary-displacement threat governing OD-1. As a peer theorem to OD-1, Theorem 2 shares OD-1's theoretical confirmation status; empirical field confirmation is pending execution of the corresponding falsification test.

title: The Game Within the Game
summary: Harassment remains a pervasive reality for many women in the workplace, yet few explicitly label their experiences as such. Instead, women often adopt alternative labels or avoid labeling altogether--a phenomenon feminist scholars call “non-labeling.” The non-labeling process, in which women make sense of and choose not to use the harassment label, is shaped by many influences, including social movements, organizational culture, and individual characteristics. Existing research conceptualizes non-labeling narrowly, often suggesting that a single factor can explain both why women avoid the harassment label and how they arrive at that decision. Drawing on 56 in-depth, semi-structured interviews with women working in the U.S. gaming (gambling) industry, my dissertation uses a feminist, constructivist grounded theory approach to examine how women navigate labeling, or not labeling, their experiences with workplace harassment. summary: La pandémie de la Covid-19 a accentué la fragilité des salariés, devenant un enjeu majeur sur le plan professionnel et social. Dans ce contexte, une équipe s’est intéressée à la prise en compte de la vulnérabilité des salariés dans les TPE et PME de la région AURA. Les chercheurs ont travaillé avec des organisations volontaires engagées pour comprendre l’origine de cette vulnérabilité, l’importance de sa prise en compte et son impact en matière d’innovation managériale. Un processus en trois étapes incluant la formalisation des représentations de la vulnérabilité, la conscientisation de cette vulnérabilité, les actions envisageables a été testé et validé par trois organisations différentes. Grâce à cette méthodologie innovante, les entreprises participantes ont mieux appréhendé la vulnérabilité de leurs salariés et ont pu concevoir des plans d’action avec une priorisation adaptée à leur structure et ainsi alimenter leur stratégie.

title: The Ontological Dominance Papers Theorem 3: The Portfolio Extension
summary: This paper states Theorem 3 of The Ontological Dominance Papers, the Portfolio Extension, governing organizations that compete across multiple product or service categories. The theorem establishes that total AI representation across a multi-category portfolio is not the unweighted average of per-category authority but the prominence-weighted average, where prominence is the fraction of total buyer queries falling into each category. The theorem specifies a quarterly monitoring and reallocation protocol and characterizes cross-category spillover as a benefit when categories share vocabulary and buyer type, and a liability when they do not. Building on the mathematical foundation in OD-S and extending OD-1, Theorem 3 was classified VERDICT B upon adversarial review: a formally correct extension of OD-1's scope conditions, not an independent theorem, confirmed by three independent mathematical derivations and contingent on OD-1's empirical field confirmation, which is pending execution.

summary: Games and Theatre have a long shared history, but are often separated along disciplinary lines. title: A Comparative Study of Narrative Techniques, Themes, and Cultural Representations in the Works of R.K. Narayan, Mulk Raj Anand, and Raja Rao
summary: ABSTRACT The paper gives a comparative literary discussion of R.K. Narayan, Mulk Raj Anand and Raja Rao- three pioneers of early Indian English literature. The paper will discuss their narrative styles, thematic interests, cultural depiction, and the contributions in general to the development of Indian writing in English. The researchers conclude that the narrative style of Narayan is characterised by simplicity, irony, and an interest in ordinary life, usually in the fictional town of Malgudi, which enables him to depict the middle-class Indian society in the form of subtle humour and humanism. title: Fighting Emotional Shrinkage : The Pain and Pleasure of Reclaiming Love in (and For) Higher Education
summary: This paper analyses reflections from a collective autoethnography on refusing to reject love in higher education. Extensive research and commentary documents an increasing instrumentalization and commercialisation of universities evident in ‘workload optimisation’, exclusive admissions and insufficient support systems, output-driven performance criteria, restrictive models of research and publication, and the encouragement of shallow pedagogical approaches. This has the un-/intended effect of what we describe as ‘emotional shrinkage’, the suppression of time, space, and inclination, for imagining and realising love for self and others. In this context, gestures of love can be understood as acts of conscious resistance. title: Description of the Male Copulatory Organ and Associated Muscles in the Quenda Isoodon fusciventer (Marsupialia: Peramelidae)
summary: Across amniotes, organs for intromission and sperm transfer show clear links between form and function. Diverse genital morphologies, deployment mechanisms and copulatory behaviours all meet the same basic requirement: delivering sperm to a receptive reproductive tract. These systems involve trade-offs between precision, time investment and likelihood of success, producing multiple mechanically distinct solutions to a shared reproductive challenge.

title: Weathering Fields:Climate, Food & Famine in History
summary: Drawing on an interdisciplinary group of leading historians, this volume presents a global set of case studies that explore the meanings people and societies have ascribed to the relationships between climate, famine events, and food supplies. Exploring modern understandings before current framings of environment and climate change, the book attends to both the diversity and local specificity of climate–food interactions, as well as how local and global conceptualisations of this relationship interconnect. From early modern Korea, to nineteenth-century Anatolia, to 1920s East Africa, the collection highlights the political nature of hunger and the impact of social interactions and power structures on historical experiences of climate, food and famine. In doing so, the book critiques current efforts to confine climate-induced hunger to the technoscientific sphere, arguing that it is only in the political and social domains that meaningful change can be achieved.

title: THREE ESSAYS ON EMPIRICAL INDUSTRIAL ORGANIZATION AND MACHINE LEARNING
summary: This dissertation investigates two critical economic challenges: global public health emergencies and the transformation of the digital economy. Through the development and application of state-of-the-art computational economics and machine learning methodologies, it provides an in-depth analysis of market behavior, policy effectiveness, and mechanism design. The dissertation consists of three independent studies within the domains of empirical industrial organization and econometrics. The first study analyzes the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic on the airline industry and consumer behavior by applying high-dimensional econometric techniques. The second study assesses the efficacy of the U.S. CARES Act on entrepreneurial entry through the synthetic control method. The third study develops a machine learning-based approach to adaptive auction mechanism design in digital markets.

title: Borrowed Shame: Hao Hongmei as a Narrative Resource for Sun Shaoping's Moral Image
summary: This article reconsiders one of the most frequently moralized episodes in Lu Yao's Ordinary World: Hao Hongmei's theft of handkerchiefs at the end of high school and Sun Shaoping's intervention on her behalf. Existing readings often treat the incident as evidence of Hao's vanity, compromised character, or eventual moral education. Such interpretations remain too close to the evaluative grammar supplied by the novel itself. Through close reading informed by affect theory, the anthropology of the gift, class analysis, and rhetorical narrative ethics, this article argues that the episode organizes a transfer of moral value. title: Critique de la raison esthétique: Phénoménologie de l’expérience esthétique et des ressorts de la création
summary: This book sets out from a commonplace: there is no disputing tastes. Far from being a thesis advanced within the debate, this maxim purports to close the debate in advance: it declares that there is nothing to be known where there is only feeling. It infers, from the de facto relativity of tastes, the absence of any validity de jure — and that inference is a paralogism. Modern physics learned not to conflate relativity with relativism: the plurality of frames of reference does not abolish objectivity but requires that it be reformulated as invariance under a regulated set of transformations. title: Repulsive media
summary: This chapter introduces repulsive media as a framework for understanding how technology and infrastructure are strategically deployed to drive people from spaces and shape normative behaviour. Drawing on affect theory, disability studies, and media history, the chapter shows how repulsion mediates both experientially, by driving bodies away, and normatively, by declaring who ought to feel unwelcome. Through a series of case studies centred on repulsive light (blue-lit bathrooms, acne-highlighting LED lightss, and glasses meant to shape appetite), the chapter develops an analysis of repulsive ambience as a political aesthetics. Repulsive media, this chapter argues, make legible the affective criteria by which bodies are moved.

title: Publishing Studies and Design Teaching: A Case Study of Interdisciplinary Teaching at University of the Arts London
summary: This reflective case study explores the intersection of publishing studies and design teaching, asking how design pedagogy can enhance publishing education. Set within an industry-facing publishing course at a creative arts university, it examines how a longstanding emphasis on design and production has developed into a distinctive specialism within practice-oriented teaching. The case study discusses experiential units that connect design and publishing through considerations of audiences, project management, content, form, and innovation. It also explores a research-led final project option that encourages design-based responses to publishing challenges, including accessibility. Two student projects investigating neurodiversity and reading are examined, alongside staff research into digital and print design, which informs teaching practice. title: Three annotated tiger beetle genomes (Coleoptera, Adephaga, Cicindelidae)
authors: Jamie Ramirez, Ming‐Hsun Chou, Grey T. Gustafson
summary: Tiger beetles are a charismatic group with ~3000 species distributed globally. Despite their popularity among insect enthusiasts and their role as bioindicators of ecosystem health, the group currently lacks a reference genome. This dataset includes genome assemblies and annotations for three tiger beetle species that span the evolutionary relationships within the lineage. Quality control analyses (BUSCO, Quast, and Referee) show that the assemblies are reference-quality and exhibit high contiguity, completeness, and accuracy. The resulting draft genome annotations will be a valuable resource for scientific endeavors and allow for continued research on tiger beetles and their allies. The attached files include assembly and annotation files for Audouin’s night-stalking tiger beetle, Omus audouini (NES728); the montane giant tiger beetle, Amblycheila baroni (NES739); and the western, red-bellied tiger beetle, Cicindelidia sedecimpunctata (NES740). summary: Professor Norrie is well known for his scholarship in relation to the children’s hearings system in Scotland, having established a body of work that is utilised consistently by students, practitioners, policy makers and courts to understand the law related to the system and its development. One of the earliest articles that Professor Norrie wrote on the children’s hearings system was In Defence of O v Rae. title: KIDS (Larry Clark, 1995)
summary: Released in 1995, Kids (dir. Larry Clark) is a film that portrays the uncompromising, unfiltered reality of New York teenagers in an environment contextualised by sex, drugs, and violence. It is the raw, pseudo-documentary style of the film and its use of non-actors that has led to resounding criticism of youth exploitation, and the film is characterised by an apparent refusal to cast any moral judgement on problematic adolescent sexuality and violent sexual relationships. This chapter aims to contextualise the controversy surrounding Kids, examining contemporaneous reviews and critical discourse amidst the release of the film, while also critiquing its enduring legacy and reassessment 30 years after its first release.

summary: “Pay careful attention to yourselves and to all the flock” (Acts 20:28) is both a warning and an invitation. It insists that the pastor's inner life and the congregation's shared life cannot be pulled apart without doing damage to both. This dissertation grows out of that conviction and out of years of pastoral ministry in Pentecostal churches where the pressure to perform often overwhelms the slow work of being formed. title: The Sexually Legible Researcher:Reflexivity, Desire, and the Politics of Being Read in Sexuality Research
summary: This article introduces the concept of the sexually legible researcher to examine how researchers are read, misread, desired, trusted, or refused within sexuality research. Moving beyond accounts of researcher positionality as something declared by the researcher, I argue that sexual legibility is relationally produced in the research encounter through embodiment, affect, disclosure, setting, and the expectations attached to sexuality as a field of knowledge. Drawing on [insert material: ethnographic vignettes/interviews/fieldnotes/reflexive episodes], the article shows how sexual legibility shapes access, rapport, ethical boundaries, analytic perception, and the forms of knowledge that become possible. Rather than treating the researcher’s sexuality as either bias, risk, or autobiographical background, the article proposes sexual legibility as a methodological problem central to sexuality research itself.

title: The World Awheel:Americans in the First Global Bicycle Age
summary: At the end of the nineteenth century, the United States was enraptured by the bicycle. The World Awheel examines this American fascination in a context of global empires and rising U.S. power. Between 1885 and 1925 many Americans understood their world at home and abroad from the perspective of a bicycle—a simple and often forgotten technology in the history of American mobility. This book argues that at a critical moment in the United States’ past, cyclists shaped American ideas of their nation in the world.From a lake in Trinidad to the American West, from major figures such as Marshall “Major” Taylor to forgotten celebrities like Fanny Bullock Workman, The World Awheel tells a global story of the American bicycle. It moves synchronically across vast geographies to understand the United States as one spoke in the first global bicycle age. summary: En el artículo se exponen nuevos y originales datos sobre el pintor Diego de Aliaga. Mencionado aunque no retratado hasta el momento por la literatura americanista en su actuación en la pequeña ciudad de Jujuy al Noroeste del virreinato del Río de la Plata. A partir de diversas y numerosas muestras documentales, elaboradas desde una perspectiva de historia social, con expedientes de archivos locales de Jujuy y nacionales de Argentina, se confirma la presencia de este pintor en la región del Tucumán y se amplía la descripción del contexto histórico e identifican otros pintores entre los menestrales. title: Writing against the machine: Postdigital resistance in LLM collaboration
summary: This chapter examines the creative and theoretical tensions that emerge when postdigital fiction authors collaborate with large language models (LLMs) trained on hegemonic discourse and structures. LLMs, designed primarily by and for dominant (cis-het white male, American corporate) perspectives, internalize and reproduce these patriarchal structures in their textual outputs. Their ever-expanding use exemplifies the postdigital, as they are integrated into daily lives and practices from autocompletion helper functions in almost all digital tools to full-on replacement of human programmers, making them ubiquitous and something more than mere “tools”. Yet creative interaction with LLMs presents a paradox for marginalized writers, particularly femme, queer, and non-Western authors, who seek to use these tools not as passive generative aids but as sites of resistance, subversion, and alternative storytelling. title: MEDICINAL PLANT USE IN UGANDA'S RWENZORI REGION
summary: This paper examines the use of medicinal plants in Kasese District, Uganda, by herbalists and the general public. To contextualize the use of medicinal plants, we asked herbalists community members about local prevalent illnesses and health practices. We also asked herbalists and community members about the plants they use and recognize. We took photographs and collected plant specimens with herbalists and asked community members to identify the plants and explain their uses. We identified approximately 95 unique medicinal plants utilized by herbalists and other community members for a wide array of conditions. The paper concludes with a discussion of possibilities for integration of herbal and biomedicines, and avenues of community-focused plant conservation.

title: Selim Al Diner 'Chaka' Nataker Bishay Bhabna O Angik Boichitra
summary: Selim Al Deen (1949-2008) is a renowned playwright and theater expert in Bangladesh. He has experimented for a long time to create the distinctive features of Bengali drama. He has shown his own uniqueness by adding a new style to the drama genre. The theatrical style he established is known as modern Bengali narrative drama. His plays reveal the ultimate expression of humanity towards people. Chaka (The wheel) is well-known among many such dramatic works by Selim Al Deen, where he attempts to decolonise Bengali theatre and drama through newer forms, structures and subject- matters. Contemporary political and social realities are intimately connected to the plot and character of this play. Also, by writing the play 'Chaka' (1991), he created a new genre called 'Kothanatya', which is a combination of drama, poetry, dance, songs, novels, fables, and storytelling.

authors: Kimberley Fowler, Emmanuele Scieri, Maxim Venetskov
summary: Codex H is a partially preserved and disassembled manuscript, held in eight collections, in seven institutions, in five countries. It is likely the earliest witness to the Euthalian tradition to the New Testament and has a complex post-production life: its entire text was re-inked, it was disbound and reused as flyleaves in multiple manuscripts, and each page preserves the imprint of the text from facing pages. Scholars have been interested in Codex H because of its connection to the Euthalian tradition and its colophon that mentions Pamphilus and the Library of Caesarea. To advance research on this important manuscript, we produced new multispectral images of most of its pages, a process that recovered twenty new pages of text that have never been transcribed and that improved transcriptions of the twenty-two other previously known transfer pages. title: Chopin’s Craft of Musical Form:Making Romantic Music with Classical Theme Types and Galant Schemata
summary: Chopin adhered to traditional practices in musical form to a far greater extent than hitherto acknowledged. He took certain standard formal paths with remarkable consistency throughout his compositional career and across almost all his favoured genres. His choices were grounded in eighteenth-century routines concerning intrathematic functions and schemata. Chopin pursued alterations and adaptations of those formal patterns, resulting in a kaleidoscopic range of variants, and in this way presented his compositions in a guise amenable to Romantic taste.
