title: Crawl & Walk
summary: 'Crawl' uses low-level drone photography to mimic the height and movement of children as they navigate the ground. This child-centered viewpoint re-enters the landscape as a site of imaginative play, improvisation, and freedom. The film is interwoven with interviews and storytelling from those who played there or who have connections to the children who did. These voices reveal the emotional and communal significance of the site, offering a vivid portrait of how informal spaces shape childhood experience. 'Walk' adopts a still, observational approach. Filmed through locked off frames, it captures the present day rewilded terrain while overlaying oral histories that recall the Millstream Way of the past—burnt out cars, makeshift dens, and a rough, unregulated environment that paradoxically nurtured creativity. The film holds past and present in tension, reflecting on what is lost when landscapes change.

summary: In a strip of post-industrial wasteland on the edge of Birmingham, a child found a world of his own. At the heart of the project is Millstream Way itself: a former industrial site in Birmingham (since transformed into a vibrant nature reserve) where Matthew Murray spent much of his childhood. He found in it a space for play, adventure, and refuge. Later, following the loss of his mother when he was twelve, the site became something more. It engages throughout the work with the idea of the ‘secret garden’: both literally, as a hidden and neglected yet magical space for childhood adventure, and metaphorically, as a place of healing, self-discovery, and growth. title: Sports Genomics Research in Turkey (2019–2026): A Systematic Review of Research Trends, Methodological Quality, and Future Directions
summary: This study aims to systematically review genetic association studies examining the relationship between genetic polymorphisms and athletic performance, injury risk, and psychological parameters in Turkish athlete populations. The review includes studies published between January 1, 2019 and April 1, 2026. Databases to be searched include PubMed, Web of Science, TRDizin, and DergiPark. The study follows PRISMA-ScR and PRISMA 2020 guidelines and includes methodological quality assessment using NIH and STREGA tools. Data synthesis will be conducted primarily using descriptive and comparative narrative analysis due to methodological heterogeneity across studies. The protocol is registered to ensure transparency, reproducibility, and methodological rigor.

authors: B. Rimington, Jack Brett, Charlie Hargood
summary: Hypertext narrative has found itself in new ludic and locative domains, where the links between content have become playful beyond mere navigation and blend realities by connecting the virtual to the real. This has proven particularly useful in the heritage domain, where hypertext offers new means of engagement to tap the narrative potential of historic sites. title: Artificial Intelligence in Plant Sciences
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) may be referred to as a family of technologies which allow computers and other machines to perform the tasks that were previously dependent on human intelligence. In order to perform the tasks autonomously, the machines learn from large volumes of input data and involve the use of machine learning algorithms. It attempts to mimic the process of human learning in which a person gradually develops knowledge and skills by continuous trial and error method. Due to the ability of AI to perform intelligent tasks, it finds a number of opportunities for application in diverse fields including plant sciences. In this chapter, let us try to gain a basic understanding of artificial intelligence and its applications with special reference to plant sciences.

title: Des valeurs en science : neutralité ou engagement ?
summary: Cette note introduit la controverse sur la nécessaire neutralité du chercheur dans sa pratique scientifique, versus son inévitable engagement éthique et social. Cette controverse ancienne donne lieu aujourd'hui à des ramifications politiques dommageables, révélatrices de tensions sociales et du rôle des sciences dans la société. Les arguments pour l'engagement ou la neutralité méritent un approfondissement, épistémologique et cognitif. Cette communication tente d'éclairer la controverse et d'ouvrir la réflexion sur le rôle des valeurs en science et leurs liens avec les impératifs d'objectivité.

title: The Truth About Judge Dredd
summary: In 2027 the British comics character Judge Dredd approaches his fiftieth anniversary. Over those five decades Dredd has seemed static - a stern, frowning, authoritarian in the midst of the madness of Mega City One - but this is not necessarily true. This presentation will compare a survey of Judge Dredd fans to the early results of a new empirical analysis of a representative sample of his appearances in 2000AD to show that what we think know about Dredd may not actually be correct. By doing so it will demonstrate why taking an empirical approach to comics studies is a surer way of producing accurate, truthful, results than our more usual methods.

title: Studies in the ancient Greek middle voice and the development of the middle participle
summary: This study examines the use and development of the Ancient Greek middle voice between the Archaic period and the Roman period, with specific focus on the aorist participle. During this time frame developments in the Greek language have been observed in scholarship which include a change in the use of voice, specifically a decrease in the use of the middle voice. Observations in scholarship also indicate a change in the use of the participle. This study demonstrates that a decrease in the use of the middle voice is not consistent across all verb forms. The findings presented are based on quantitative data collected using chosen verbs and verb forms found in Greek texts between the Archaic and Roman period. Through this research the participle, infinitive, and finite forms are found to behave differently to each other. title: From Texts to Contradictions: The Triple Connotation of Marx’s “Real Movement” and the Dynamic Convergence of Communism
summary: In The German Ideology, Marx writes that “communism is the real movement which abolishes the existing state of things.” This passage is often quoted but rarely explored in its layered meanings. Many reduce it to a simple slogan: communism is a process. This paper offers a close reading of Marx’s proposition. It identifies three interconnected connotations. First, the proposition rejects utopian statics. Marx denies that communism is “a state of affairs to be established” or “an ideal to which reality must conform.” In doing so, he distances himself from both idealist socialism and Young Hegelian critique. Second, communism rests on material premises. The conditions of the movement arise from existing premises: productive forces, division of labor, class antagonisms. Third, communism is a process without a final terminus. The abolition of the existing state of things is not a single act. It is an ongoing historical movement. title: RESEARCH UNDER PRESSURE: IMPACTFUL INDUSTRYACADEMIC COLLABORATION IN AN ACCELERATED DIGITAL WORLD
summary: While industry-academic collaboration has always been challenging, the current environment introduces new and intensifying pressures. Rapid career turnover among industry partners makes sustaining long-term relationships difficult, while organisations increasingly expect quick, tangible outcomes. At the same time, global dynamics shape research priorities and funding, placing noticeable pressures on areas such as inclusion and diversity. Academic incentives further complicate collaboration as top-tier journals often prioritise theoretical over practical contributions. The rapid rise of generative AI adds both opportunity and instability to partnership building. This panel addresses two key challenges: how to establish and sustain meaningful collaborations among academia, industry, and policymakers in a fast-changing context, and how to translate these collaborations into outputs that are both academically rigorous and relevant to practice.

summary: Book synopsis: Birgittine Acts of Memory begins from a simple but insistent premise: memory is not something that is stored, but something that happens. Focusing on the Birgittine Order across late medieval Europe, modern Europe, and contemporary spaces, the volume explores how remembrance takes shape through gestures, materials, voices, and spaces. Moving beyond static notions of preservation, it approaches memory as an active, embodied, and relational process, entangled with questions of authority, devotion, and communal life, and unfolding across liturgy, objects, and affective practices. Bringing together interdisciplinary contributions, the book moves across manuscripts, liturgical performance, visual culture, queer theory, and testamentary bequests, attending to the acts that sustain and transform memory. title: Home
summary: A short lyric-philosophical meditation on the meanings of "home." Beginning with the way every creature names home as a series of widening circles — nest, tree, house, city, country, sky — the piece asks what humanity is finally rising toward, and whether the answer lies outward at all. Drawing on ideas of dwelling as belonging, of home as a way of being woven into the world, and of an old homesickness that no journey resolves, it reframes that longing not as a problem to be solved but as evidence of a home already carried within. Part of an ongoing series of philosophical prose.

title: Long shadows in the gallery: George Watson Taylor as collector, connoisseur and slave-owner
summary: Over the course of the 1820s, as British slave-owners were drawn increasingly into a bitter and contested debate about the future of slavery, the nation’s art institutions were thriving. The foundation of a National Gallery in 1824 was the culmination of several decades of lobbying from various quarters, and the concomitant rise of private collections in Britain. The wealth and confidence of British art collectors and connoisseurs in the period is amply demonstrated in a grand painting by Dutch artist Pieter Christoffel Wonder, Patrons and Lovers of Art (1830). title: Chemoenzymatic Synthesis of Verruculogens and Mechanistic Studies of FtmOx1
summary: Verruculogens are fumitremorgin alkaloids that contain an unusual eight-membered endoperoxide ring attached to a fused pentacyclic core. Due to their potent bioactivity and unusual structures, this family of compounds has attracted significant interest from the synthetic community. Using enzymatic C−H peroxidation and rhodium-catalyzed C−C bond activation, we were able install the eight-membered endoperoxide and the pentacyclic core of the natural product, 13-oxoverruculogen. Central to this route was the use of 13-epi-fumitremorgin B as the first substrate analog to be endoperoxidated by verruculogen synthase (FtmOx1). To further assess the native substrate promiscuity, we synthesized and subjected numerous substrate analogs to FtmOx1 for endoperoxidation. Additionally, using our established route, we synthesized isotope-labeled analogs of FtmOx1’s native substrate, fumitremorgin B, to probe the mechanism of endoperoxidation.

title: Miracle babies: historical narratives as windows into babies’ social and spiritual lives
summary: Babies rarely appear as historical subjects in their own right, but tend to be presented as adults-in-waiting or as blank slates for the projection of contemporary ideas about childhood. This problem is compounded when researching the Middle Ages, because high infant mortality rates mean that many babies have left little historical record; moreover, a dominant historical interpretation has emphasised parents’ cost-benefit analysis for investing emotional, social and material resources in babies whose survival was always in question. To challenge these perspectives, this chapter attempts to write a history which centres a baby and his interactions with the society and culture around him. I present a miracle story from late sixth-century Tours (modern France) which, read in its historical context, allows us to identify the creation of social connections and the development of social institutions to provide spiritual and physical sustenance for babies. title: Un espace de renouvellement des pratiques: le Laboratoire de cartographie/graphique de la VIe section de l'EPHE/EHESS (1948-2000)
summary: This research aims to trace the history of the Cartography and Graphics Laboratory, established within the Sixth Section of the EPHE, named EHESS since 1975. Through the analysis of unpublished archival material and interviews, this Laboratory emerges as a unique space for the renewal of practices in the social sciences field. By fully integrating manipulation into the heuristic process and developing a theory of graphic semiology, the laboratory challenges questions of the division and hierarchisation of knowledge, and the split between thought and technique, between knowledge and know-how.

title: A Prolonged Genocide: The Sterilization and Castration Experiences of Hungarian Jews and Roma in National Socialist Camps
summary: The dissertation examines the lasting impact of sterilization and castration experiments endured by Jewish and Romani victims in the National Socialist concentration camps of Auschwitz, Birkenau, and Lackenbach. It documents wartime atrocities but centers primarily on the postwar repercussions and the enduring physiological, psychological, and social effects these procedures had on survivors’ lives. To capture these extended harms, the dissertation introduces the concept of prolonged genocide, defined as the continuation of genocidal violence beyond the moment of survival through lasting bodily damage, reproductive loss, social marginalization, and silenced suffering.

title: Spectral Materialism: Encounters with land-time-scapes
summary: This transdisciplinary, practice-based PhD introduces spectral materialism through art-based research encounters with ecologically and historically stratified land-time-scapes shaped by hypersalinity and colonial terraforming. Centred in the semi-arid Mallee (southeastern Australia) and read through echoes with California’s Imperial Valley, the project examines how spectral time—the co-presence and haunting of other temporalities—manifests in the material conditions of salt, soil, water, plants, and infrastructures. It asks how learning from geological, First Nations, colonial, and ecological pasts can orient responsibilities in unsettled futures. Treating the present as a crisis of time as much as a crisis of matter, the thesis critiques linear-progressive temporalities bound to Western modernity and extractive regimes. summary: Silver grounds the magic of analogue photography; it is the essential light-sensitive element of photographic negatives. Silver exists in specific territories and is mobilised across the globe to enable media culture, and we live in a critical time where media culture and pollution are affecting people and places in disproportionate ways. title: Realism and the Romantic Essay: Source Studies of Victorian Prose
summary: This book discusses the importance of the Romantic essay to the development of realism in the Victorian era. It explores how specific texts by key Victorian authors—Dickens, Ruskin, Eliot, Pater, Hardy, and Stevenson—depart from the principles and practice of their forebears in prose: William Hazlitt, Leigh Hunt, and Charles Lamb. Reviving, in its methodology, a now nearly obsolete critical mode, the source study, it tracks in the transition from essayists of the Romantic era to their Victorian successors, a changing relation between 'ideal' and 'real', or 'self' and 'other'. Naming as 'realism', an English literary practice of the nineteenth century that, mimetic in its expression, remains committed to the absolute and uncompromised reality of the other, it argues for the importance of the Romantic essay to the genesis and evolution of this practice. summary: The emerging literature on ‘generative justice’ has tended to focus on the solidarity of reintegrative communities after punishment (McNeill, 2024,, cf Grossi, 2024, Cohen and Winemiller, 2026; McGowan and Perrin, 2026). summary: This thesis argues that Russian human rights defenders’ responses to the Foreign Agents’ Law reveal a polyvocal and context-dependent legal consciousness that challenges the universal applicability of dominant legal consciousness frameworks. By putting legal culture and legal consciousness approaches into dialogue, it re-theorises legal consciousness outside the North American context, showing how Russian activists simultaneously reproduce and resist dominant legal meanings to generate a more situated understanding of law’s role under increasing authoritarianism. Introduced in 2012, the Foreign Agents’ Law regulates non-profit organisations based on funding sources and activities. Over the next decade, it became a central tool of civil society repression, particularly targeting human rights organisations. title: Socio-semiotics and the history of "working-class comics and cartoons" in Sweden
summary: In the following, I will first relate how certain graphic works of autofiction have come to be accepted as contributions to the tradition of working-class literature in Sweden. Then I will exemplify how some of these works could be analysed from a socio-semiotic point of view, drawing some inspiration from Bruce Campbell’s studies of the political use of comics in Mexico. Lastly, I will sketch the outlines of a Swedish history of cartooning aimed at a working-class audience, and repose the following question, which I regard to be socio-semiotic in essence: Are simple artistic means and deskilling a visual marker of grassroot authenticity, and is it even a decisive semiotic choice for cartoonists who want to be associated with working-class autofiction, leftist politics and labour history?

Drawing upon workers’ oral history interview testimonies and other personal accounts (including online reminiscence forums) this essay comments on how smell is remembered and narrated by occupational communities. title: I Call You My Love
summary: ‘I call you my love’ contains an extended, years-long correspondence exchanged between lovers Sunil Gupta and Steve Dodd from the mid-‘80s to the early ‘90s. During this time, Steve was completing his PhD in America while Sunil worked in London, and their frequent and detailed letters are a testament to the strength of their transatlantic romantic connection. In addition to the letters, this publication includes photographs of the couple, taken by Sunil, alongside ephemera from their written exchanges — envelopes, poetry, sketches, and newspaper clippings. The book also features a collaborative series, “Pretended” Family Relationships, composed of Sunil’s photographs and accompanied by lines from one of Steve’s poems.

summary: This major survey exhibition will reveal Sunil Gupta’s (b.1953, New Delhi) pioneering contribution to photography over five decades. Intimate, subversive and often beautiful, Gupta’s work has been instrumental in raising awareness around the fight for queer rights internationally, particularly in India and the UK, laying bare the tensions between tradition and modernity, and public and private spheres. Gupta’s love for family, friends and partners, and his belief that everyone has the right to lead full and joyful lives – in which identity and sexuality can be celebrated without fear – shines throughout his work. title: Art-Based Emotional Regulation Through an Occupational Lens
summary: Emotional dysregulation is common among children in outpatient therapy, affecting up to 20% of youth ages 0–19, with prevalence increasing to 33% in outpatient settings and 67% in mental health settings (Baroud, 2024; Haeyen, 2020). Contributing factors include adverse childhood experiences, anxiety, trauma, and symptoms of mental health and developmental disorders (Beiderman, 2019; Moehler, 2022; Paulus, 2021). This project aims to address gaps in literature by identifying effective art-based interventions for emotional regulation. It does so through a program designed to educate outpatient pediatric clinicians and explore practical strategies to support clients experiencing emotional dysregulation. Overall, this study synthesizes the effectiveness of art-based interventions as a tool for emotional regulation. Keywords: Emotional, Regulation, Pediatrics, Art-Based, Intervention

title: A collaborative and participatory approach to public service innovation: Health sector dynamics and outlook
authors: Fatima Yatim, Alan Sitkin, Cadenza Academic Translations
summary: This article explores the dynamics of collaborative and participatory innovations in public health services using Chen et al.’s (2020) typology. Based on a mixed survey of projects awarded under the national “Droits des usagers de la santé” initiative, the study finds that user participation primarily generates operational and capacity-oriented innovations frequently involving external partnerships. The analysis highlights the crucial interactions between internal and external dynamics, identifying essential conditions for successful innovations: effective mobilization of internal resources, robust institutional support, and early and active user involvement. However, the study also identifies limitations in citizen engagement, particularly in the evaluation phase of innovations. The article concludes by suggesting avenues for enhancing full co-creation processes in public services to maximize public value.

title: Unveiling the Dynamics of Super Apps: Adoption Factors and Strategic Insights across Key Industries
authors: Jan Budinský, Mohit Srivastava, Heřman Kopkáně, Ladislav Tyll, Ladislav Tyll
summary: This study examined the emerging phenomenon of super apps, which are comprehensive platforms transforming mobile applications worldwide. It expanded the focus beyond mobility-based super apps to analyze their adoption across five critical sectors: mobility, food delivery and mobility, messaging, fintech, and e-commerce. Using logistic regression models on a dataset of 1,783 enterprises, of which 43 were classified as super apps, the study identified key factors that influence super app adoption. More specifically, this research fills a significant gap in the literature on platforms and multi-sided markets by evaluating the strategic development of super apps from a multisectoral perspective. In addition, it presents a conceptual framework for analyzing the technological infrastructure, regulatory landscape, market economics, and competition, as well as the network effects and multi-sided market dynamics that influence the growth trajectories of super apps. summary: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is characterized by a steep decline in the recall of recent memories and events. It has previously been shown that elevated levels of intracellular tau-containing tangles (tau) are associated with greater risks of AD-related memory deficits. title: Speak To me, I'm Listening
summary: Composed for dual cassette Speak To Me, I'm Listening explores the use of cassette and cassette player's as both compositional tools and performance medias. Countering production and recording methods that offer endless multitracking the work explores the linearity of single track cassette tape as a way to reimagine multi-tracked arrangements. Working across two cassettes and two cassette players the work reimagines mutlti-tracking as a spatialised process emerging via the very medias in which the work was recorded and performed. The work was part of the SoundArts Lab residency in Struer, Denmark.

summary: Illustrators are increasingly connecting with community groups and members of the public to explore links between people, local knowledge and image making practices. This raises a number of questions: What processes are set in motion when illustrators seek to engage with community? How can illustration bring to light the concerns, interests and challenges of a group of people? And can illustration help us think about the conditions of sociability more generally? Luise Vormittag argues that these questions go to the core of what it means to be political. Using both her own work and other illustrators’ projects as case studies Vormittag suggests that participatory illustration is a particularly effective medium for illuminating and reflecting on our social interdependence. title: Ruskin and the Science of Colour
summary: This chapter examines John Ruskin’s engagement with the colour blue, exploring its aesthetic, symbolic, scientific, and emotional significance in his work. Divided into two sections, the first analyses Ruskin’s theoretical perspectives on blue, as expressed in his lectures and critical texts; while the second section shifts to Ruskin’s practical advice for artists, particularly on the technical challenges of depicting blue in painting. Using analytical techniques, the study examines blue pigments in artworks from Ruskin’s university teaching collections at Oxford, Lancaster, and Harvard, and situates his radical ideas within nineteenth-century debates on colour in art, architecture, science, and the natural world. By exploring Ruskin’s influence on art, science, and philosophy, this chapter underscores his role as a mediator between tradition and innovation, revealing his lasting impact on colour theory and perception.

title: The Ember Records and archival elegy
summary: The archival elegy is a concept that I arrived at through the initial drafts of my creative work for The Ember Records, my poetry collection written as part of this thesis. In writing numerous elegies for late friends and family members, I began to wonder about the mechanics and the purposes of the elegy itself. What I learned is that when we mourn the dead through the elegy, we are using textual traces to memorialise them, essentially preserving their memories in the face of death’s destructiveness. The elegy is built on this knife-edge of memory and oblivion, and this is how I arrived at the idea of the elegy being a form of archive. This novel concept is important because it dismantles many of our existing notions of what an archive can be. As I shall explore later through the writings of thinkers such as Jacques Derrida, Sadiya Hartman, Ann Cvetkovich, and many others, the archive cannot be conceived exclusively as a physical or digital space in which various historical documents a...

title: Bending and breaking the boundary between horror and comedy: an exploration of the existentialist function of the abject in the works of John Landis and Woody Allen
summary: This thesis explores the line between comedy and horror in an increasingly postmodern world through the cinema of John Landis and Woody Allen. Chapter One explores the theoretical and historical material that link Landis and Allen, namely in their dealing with (1) Edgar Allan Poe’s effect, (2) Julia Kristeva and Judith Butler’s abject, (3) Sigmund Freud’s “uncanny,” and (4) Mikhail Baktin’s carnivalesque. The chapter will conclude with John Landis’ portions of The Twilight Zone: The Movie, as a linked history that welcomes exploration of Landis alongside Allen. Chapter Two conducts a comparative study of two horror-comedies: John Landis’ An American Werewolf in London (1981) and Woody Allen’s Shadows and Fog (1991). Chapter Three explores Allen’s Alice (1990) and Deconstructing Harry (1997) to posit a potential method for future creations of horror-comedies. title: Mid-Twentieth-Century Women Writers: Country House Fiction from Elizabeth Bowen to Ivy Compton-Burnett
summary: The country house is one of the crucial sites in anglophone fiction published just before and after World War II. Each of my chapters converges on a different author – Elizabeth Bowen, Elizabeth Taylor, Ivy Compton-Burnett and Barbara Comyns – to explore how their novels represent species of spaces and class hierarchies in the ancestral mansion or Anglo-Irish ‘big house’. Why these four authors in particular? First, they read, admired and promoted one another’s work. In her regular ‘Book Reviews’ column for The Tatler magazine, Bowen discussed new novels by Taylor, Compton-Burnett and Comyns. Taylor’s attitude to Bowen’s fiction was one of ‘blinkered devotion’, according to Taylor’s biographer Nicola Beauman. Compton-Burnett and Taylor were also friends; their correspondence affords a fascinating glimpse into their narrative strategies and recreational reading habits. title: Soil Politics
summary: This thesis investigates soil as a political material, which has been mobilised as an environmental laboratory to enable the transition from colonial forms of power towards late liberal governance. From the perspective of what I term “soil politics,” colonisation operates through the land, and continues to materialise in the present with the modification of soil’s chemical properties. In particular, I focus my research project on the global soil surveys initiated after the Second World War by the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) as a defining moment in the transformation of land from earthly matter into a techno-scientific assemblage, invested with the capacity to unsettle and reorganise modes of life. summary: This thesis intervenes in current academic debates on the translation of cultural elements from Arabic into English by examining the translation histories of two major Arabic novels that achieved recognition in the Anglophone world. title: The Book of Architecture of John Thorpe in Sir John Soane’s Museum, London: c.1596-c.1623
summary: The Book of Architecture of John Thorpe (c.1565-1655) consists of some 295 drawings ranging primarily from the 1590s to the 1620s and covering 168 buildings, mainly but not only English, and amongst the greatest of the period. The drawings include plans, elevations, some full-size sections of mouldings, and a depiction of the five orders derived from Hans Blum’s 1550 treatise on the orders. Bound in a hard cover in the 18th c., since 1810 the album has been preserved in one of London’s most iconic museums of British architecture, created by the celebrated architect Sir John Soane (1753-1837), who added to the album with about six sketches of his own. Alongside new catalogue entries featuring digital copies of the drawings in colour, enlargeable, and uncut, my edition will include a c.40.000-word critical analysis addressing all aspects above-mentioned. summary: In accordance with the principles of imitatio and aemulatio Derzhavin saw himself not only as a translator of Horace, but also as an Horatian poet in his own right. Reading Horace not in Latin, but in German, modifying this tradition under the specific conditions of eighteenth-century Russian culture as well as of his personal inclinations. title: The Open River Network (ORN) - a topologically correct and attributed open-source river network for Great Britain
summary: This talk presents a topologically correct, attributed, analysis-ready river network for Great Britain. It is built from the OS Open River (TM), an Open Data released under an Open Government License (OGL). The original release of OS Open Rivers was not a fully connected dataset limiting its use in analysis and research. The OS Open Rivers data underwent extensive editing to correct and enforce a full network geospatial dataset to become the Open River Network (ORN). As a fully connected network, it was possible to run tools to attribute the network, generate a sampling point layer of over 1.4 million points and build a catchment layer linking over 1.2 million quality-controlled catchment areas to their sampling point. The true power of ORN, a richly attributed dataset, is its ability to be exploited through automation. The next release of ORN will include floodplain width transects for the whole of GB.

title: The Decadent Fairy Tale: Queering the Othered Body, 1880-1920
summary: Decadent writers and artists repeatedly drew inspiration from the fairy tale, and reworked the fairy tale into a subversive and experimental adult text. This thesis is the first doctoral study to explore Renée Vivien (Pauline Mary Tarn) and Althea Gyles as writers of decadent fairy tales, and will investigate how Vivien, Gyles, Oscar Wilde, Laurence Housman and Harry Clarke recognized and utilized the potential of the fairy tale to encode subversive representations of the othered body. Such representations have a dual function, in both highlighting the physical alterity present in the fairy tale, and providing a powerful metaphor to communicate experiences of sexual difference. title: Provoking Public Reflection on Robotics and AI through Cat Royale, an Artistic Installation
authors: Eike Schneiders, Steve Benford, Kate Devlin, Alan Chamberlain, Joel Fischer
summary: Current discussion on AI often presents binary for/against stances, making it difficult to foster nuanced discourse. But how can we as designers, developers, researchers, and artists communicate the nuances of our work to non-experts? Art can be a powerful medium for public engagement prompting reflection on complex topics. We examine audience engagement with Cat Royale, an artwork that invited audiences to reflect on AI, robotics, and the trust we place in them. We show that constructing and presenting an art installation as a deliberately ambiguous interface can provoke and encourage critical reflection, and we argue for the importance of making abstract technologies, such as AI, tangible and relatable through concrete examples, including artworks. Finally, we examine forms of ambiguity that arise at the intersection of AI and public engagement, and propose two new kinds relevant to the future of beyond-human interaction in HCI: moral ambiguity and ambiguity of species.

title: Experiencing Shakespeare's Theatres:Playgoing, Pleasure and Judgement in Early Modern England
summary: In this transformative study, Simon Smith explores how playwrights like Shakespeare crafted their plays for demanding and varied commercial audiences. Rediscovering the many forms of judgement practiced in the early modern playhouse, he investigates influences ranging from the classical tradition and grammar-school classroom to ballad and jest culture. Where many prior studies have treated 'the judicious' as a self-contained subset of playgoers, Smith reveals the variety of careful assessments made in the theatre by a wide range of playgoers, showing that judgement and pleasure were often simultaneous elements of the same response. Chapters examine specific parts of plays that were especially subject to evaluation and generative of enjoyment: spectacle, words, plot, and actorly technique. Close readings shed fresh light on much-studied plays like Hamlet and Volpone, as well as exploring several unfairly overlooked plays. title: Succession dans les Petites et Moyennes Entreprises (PME) familiales camerounaises : quel rôle des stratégies comportementales dans le processus d’intégration des successeurs ?
summary: In the literature on family business succession, few studies have focused on the exploration of behavioral strategies. The aim of this study is to provide a better understanding of the role played by behavioral strategies in the process of integrating successors into family SMEs. This exploratory study required the adoption of a qualitative methodology. It focused on four cases of Cameroonian family SMEs. The analysis, carried out between 2023 and 2024 and improved in 2025, shows that successful integration requires the transformation of the successor, the implementation of objective exchanges, and the establishment of relationships between the successor and the company’s various stakeholders. In concrete terms, the results of this study show that relational, transformational and transactional strategies facilitate the acceptance of successors and enable them to acquire credibility and legitimacy with the various stakeholders. The results achieved contribute to the literature on unders...

title: « Jouer dans la vie réelle » : Enrôler des professionnels pour mieux engager les étudiants dans l’apprentissage de compétences commerciales
summary: How to introduce the most realistic situations possible in the context of university teaching ? How to enroll professionals in the evaluation of students’ development in business skills ? The following article describes an educational innovation based on gamification and regular communication of a study project with professionals. It proposes a theoretical framework to evaluate this approach. The students’ appreciation of their business skills is an important issue in the last year of their bachelor’s degree, as a condition for a successful entry into a master’s degree in apprenticeship. But this self-marketing assumes that they feel legitimate to claim professional skills, especially when they do not have previously related work experience. Being able to associate professionals with a pedagogical project and allow them to be witnesses of the students’ progress is a lever to improve the perceived legitimacy of students to claim their skills and achievements. We show that the theory of ...

title: Exploring the Entrepreneurial Intentions of Academic Inventors in an Emerging Context: The Case of Morocco
summary: This study investigates the entrepreneurial intentions of academic inventors in Morocco, an emerging economy where the establishment of university-based ventures remains exceptionally rare, despite a notable increase in patenting activity within Moroccan universities over the past decade. Based on 16 semi-structured interviews, the research applies thematic content analysis (TCA) to identify the key factors that shape these intentions. The findings highlight that, beyond legal, financial, and structural challenges, inventors’ perceptions and beliefs about the business world, their academic roles, and their professional identities deeply influence entrepreneurial intentions. In particular, those identified as “unintentional inventors” demonstrate a strong emotional commitment to their academic mission, hold ambiguous or conflicting relationships with money, and perceive entrepreneurship as fundamentally incompatible with their professional roles. JEL Codes: L26, O31, O31, O34.

title: Le jeu de rôle ludique : un terrain d’analyse et d’entraînement pour l’acquisition de compétences managériales
summary: Unlike serious role-playing games, which attempt to simulate certain situations and interactions in the business world, tabletop role-playing games set their narrative in a fictional universe. RPG games provide an excellent opportunity to analyse the interaction and thinking patterns of participants and offers the possibility to develop new behaviours and testing them over the course of one or more game sessions, using the “decontextualised” simulation system on a benevolent testing ground, an immersive simulation environment that enables analysis and personal growth work. This activity has been the subject of workshops run by PsychoStratégie SA, which constitute a case study showing how tabletop RPGs can be used in an innovative way to develop the managerial skills of professionals through a deeper understanding of their own interactional and reflexive patterns and the development of new behaviours and tactics.

title: Le projet design comme moyen de stimuler l’intention entrepreneuriale
summary: Entrepreneurship is a complex process initiated by an intention that leads to business creation. In Tunisia, it plays an essential role in the employability of young graduates and contributes to economic growth. Design, a creative discipline based on active project pedagogy, provides fertile ground for innovation and entrepreneurship. This research examines the extent to which project-based pedagogy in design and the ESSTED ecosystem foster the emergence of entrepreneurial intention. The study adopts a qualitative exploratory approach, based on semi-structured interviews with ten graduates who became entrepreneurs, supplemented by a thematic analysis. The results reveal internal and external factors influencing this intention. The experience of institutional projects, structured around Design Thinking and project-based pedagogy, appears as a major lever for developing the skills, attitudes, and aptitudes necessary for entrepreneurship. JEL Codes : A22, O35, M12, M14

title: Intention entrepreneuriale : profils et vision stratégique. Étude de cas des étudiants algériens
summary: The objective of this paper is twofold: on the one hand, it aims to develop a typology of individuals’ entrepreneurial intentions based on the level of intention, the maturity of that intention, and entrepreneurial desirability; on the other hand, it analyses entrepreneurial intention from a strategic perspective by exploring how individuals shape their intentions according to their vision of future actions, and by examining the actions envisaged within the context of their entrepreneurial project. To this end, the study is based on the case of Master’s students at the University of Bejaia (Algeria). The findings reveal, firstly, the existence of various intention profiles; secondly, they indicate that entrepreneurial intentions are shaped by the vision one develops of opportunities, resources, goals, and entrepreneurial challenges. Although the components of this vision vary from group to group, a general trend emerges: a focus on autonomy, entrepreneurial individualism, an emphasis o...

title: L’intention entrepreneuriale des femmes rurales en agroécologie au Sénégal : initiative personnelle ou influence des ONG ?
summary: This article analyzes the entrepreneurial intention of rural women engaged in agroecology in Senegal, distinguishing their intrinsic motivations from the influence exerted by non-governmental organizations (NGOs). Based on one hundred biographical interviews conducted with women members of Women’s Promotion Groups (Groupements de promotion féminine, GPF) in the Fatick region, this research examines how individual aspirations, sociocultural constraints, and institutional support interact to shape this entrepreneurial intention. The findings reveal that their engagement stems both from personal aspirations (income diversification, promotion of local knowledge) and from the support provided by NGOs. The study concludes by emphasizing the necessity of simultaneously strengthening individual capacities and collective dynamics to prevent any institutional dependence and ensure the sustainability of their agroecological projects. JEL Codes : Z130.

title: Pratiques ludiques dans les armées françaises à un moment d’évolution de la conflictualité
summary: Wargaming (or wargame practice) within the French armed forces has undergone a structural revival since 2022, as an imperative response to the changing nature of conflict. This dynamic, initially rooted in educational gaming within training schools, has gradually become institutionalized as a tool for strategic analysis and operational planning support, with each component of the French armed forces adapting this tool to its own challenges and needs. Thus, 2023 marks a major turning point with the creation of a dedicated entity within the Armed Forces Staff, aimed at strengthening “human interoperability” and debate among senior decision-makers. Paradoxically, manual/physical gaming remains the preferred method for exploring the impact of technological breakthroughs on the theater of operations, simulating digital (cyber) confrontations, and identifying cognitive biases in crisis situations. There is now also a “French Touch” in the field of professional military game design, supported...

title: Les déterminants du succès du programme d’accompagnement de l’intention entrepreneuriale
authors: Sorelle Gertrude Ngoungoure Ngouloure, Bertin Léopold Kouayep
summary: The poor results of entrepreneurial education programs have led the State of Cameroon to establish the National Status of the Student-Entrepreneur. The objective of this article is to highlight the factors that influence the success of this program in Cameroon. The mobilization of previous studies and entrepreneurial theory through effectuation revealed the key success factors that the State could integrate during the implementation of the program. These include the necessity of establishing a network operation and developing partnerships between private companies and all entities involved in the program. JEL Codes : O55, L26

title: L’innovation locale et sa contribution au développement durable : pour une taxonomie du système local de transition
summary: L’article examine l’innovation locale en l’opposant au modèle schumpétérien, centré sur le marché, qui aborde les territoires uniquement dans le cadre de la compétition mondiale. Envisager l’innovation au service du développement durable du territoire implique de l’intégrer dans la politique de transition écologique. L’article propose de dépasser la notion de système local d’innovation pour envisager celle de système local de transition, dont les composantes seront développées. Pour cela, nous nous attacherons dans un premier temps à considérer quels types d’innovation sont envisagés au-delà de la technologie : innovations systémiques, éco-innovations et innovations sociales et culturelles. L’article considérera ensuite le rôle particulier que jouent les institutions du territoire, ainsi que les connaissances locales et scientifiques. Il examine quels leviers les collectivités peuvent mobiliser en identifiant les différents moteurs de l’innovation. Enfin, il considérera les moyens de s...

title: Mécanismes internes de gouvernance et internationalisation : quelles leçons pour les moyennes entreprises à capitaux camerounais ?
authors: Gildas Alex KENGNI FOMO, Sigismond Hervey Mvele
summary: The objective of this study is to identify the effect of internal governance mechanisms on the internationalization decisions decision of medium-sized enterprises in Cameroon. To achieve this, data were collected from a survey of 136 medium-sized enterprises located in the Littoral and Central regions between 2017 and 2020. Analysis of these data using Sargan tests, autocorrelation tests and generalized method of moments (GMM) regression revealed that the presence of independent external directors, board size, and dual board structure positively and significantly influence the international development of medium-sized enterprises in Cameroon. Conversely, capital concentration and the presence of institutional investors do not affect the international expansion decisions of the companies in the sample. These results corroborate those of Fredrich et al. (2022) and Bužavaitė and Korsakienė (2022), and confirm the contribution of board characteristics to the internationalization decision-m...

title: Comprendre les effets rebonds circulaires et innover pour les atténuer
summary: Despite local successes, the circular economy has not yet succeeded in significantly reducing the consumption of virgin raw materials or environmental impacts on a global scale. Among many other causes, the notion of the circular economy rebound effect has recently been introduced to account for this shortcoming, although it remains relatively underexplored. This leads to two questions: “How do rebound effects manifest themselves in the circular economy?” and “How can these rebound effects be mitigated to achieve strong sustainability?” Drawing on a metanarrative literature review, this article provides an up-to-date synthesis of theoretical contributions to better understand the phenomenon of circular economy rebound effects. By cross-referencing critical studies on the circular economy, work advocating various forms of innovation and principles aligned with strong sustainability, the article also suggests five practical avenues to mitigate them across several systemic levels. JEL Cod...

title: L’apport de l’informalité de l’économie sociale et solidaire à la mise en œuvre de l’économie circulaire
summary: We can make informality a strong concept that allows us to discuss the problems of regulating the dominant economy in its search for more sustainable development. The informality of the circular economy intersects the economy and the environment with the aim of achieving the ecological pillar of sustainable development, while the social economy intersects the economy and the social to achieve the equitable pillar. In this paper, we defend the hypothesis that the informality of the social economy will contribute to the circular economy while one might think the opposite. A learning dynamic can then be established between the two types of economy. We will validate this hypothesis by analyzing the case of an incubator open to social entrepreneurship and two structures for integration through economic activity. JEL Codes : L31, M21, Q57

title: Une étude a posteriori de la construction de l’intention entrepreneuriale chez les entrepreneurs agricoles d’Afrique subsaharienne
summary: The literature on entrepreneurial intention has mostly examined the factors capable of predicting entrepreneurial action, and rarely those that actually led to it. This research therefore focuses on the factors that favored the transition to entrepreneurial action, in the specific context of Sub-Saharan Africa, and within the specific sector of agriculture. Using two embedded case studies, and within a comprehensive approach, we examine the ex-post influence of the 3 components of the theory of planned behavior on the entrepreneurial decision. Social norms are the least influential component, due to the lack of positive recognition for entrepreneurs and agriculture. Personal attitude, a favorable component, highlights the roles of family and academic education. Finally, the behavioral control component positively influences the transition to actio through preparation and extended stay in the informal mode, which turns out to be a genuine strategic choice.

summary: This exhibition presents artwork from AZUKI, the upcoming graphic novel by EIU alum Kofi Bazzell‑Smith. AZUKI is a wacky action‑comedy set in a world where Rock, Paper, Scissors is a full‑fledged martial art, complete with over‑the‑top techniques and ridiculous battles. Drawing from Kofi’s background in manga and martial arts, the project mixes sharp action, big humor, and a blend of Black and East Asian cultural influences that shape Azuki’s world. On display are pages and behind‑the‑scenes process sketches that show how the story and visual style of AZUKI are coming together.

title: Contours of Duration: Movement Authored Through Form—A Behavior Archive
summary: Insect anatomy offers an elegant example of motion derived from structure. Inspired by insect movement, Contours of Duration employs a cam-and-follower system consisting of moving, leg-like parts, designed to engage a series of rotating cams, such that the shape of each cam’s surface activates the legs in unique ways, generating repetitive movement, and demonstrating how geometry produces distinct motion behaviors over time. Through iterative experimentation and controlled variation, trace emerges as a central methodology, whereby movement, over time, creates a distinct pattern of marks, making motion legible and reflecting how subtle changes to surface and form generate different behavioral outcomes. As the research develops, trace becomes central not only as a record of motion, but as a design tool for reading, comparing, and understanding behavior over time. summary: This research aimed to assess the employees’ appraisal on their work productivity within Aljamea-tus-Saifiyah Campus, Nairobi County, Kenya. title: Exploring the Abilities and Limitations of the SARIMA Model For Retail Demand Forecasting on Dillard’s Data From 2021-2025
summary: Retail demand forecasting is important for businesses such as Dillard’s, a leading American department store chain, because it allows for data-driven decisions that enhances profitability, efficiency, and customer satisfaction. These forecasts serve as a strategic foundation for various business aspects from inventory management and supply chain planning to marketing campaigns and more. Forecasting methods vary widely from traditional to advanced machine learning models, each offering their pros and cons. This thesis will explore the ability and limitations of the seasonal autoregressive integrated (SARIMA) model to forecast demand on nearly four years of product group data provided by Dillard’s.

title: Iron-Catalyzed 1,2-trans-β-selective Glycosylations for Rapid Glycosaminoglycan Assembly
summary: Chemical synthesis of certain glycosaminoglycans like hyaluronic acid and chondroitin sulfate has long been challenging due to critical synthetic intermediates lacking in reactivity and inhibiting stereoselectivity. New methodology for the stereoselective formation of 1,2-trans</em>-β glycosidic bonds via catalysis with a hemin</em>-derived iron porphyrin triflate complex has been developed, allowing for the use of hindered secondary glycosyl acceptors and electron deficient glycosyl donors. This expanded substrate scope has made hyaluronic acid and chondroitin sulfate not only synthetically accessible but capable of rapid assembly with several glycosylations. Herein, syntheses of disaccharide components for hyaluronic acid and chondroitin sulfate syntheses via iron-catalyzed 1,2-trans</em>-β-selective glycosylation is reported, alongside progress towards tetrasaccharide syntheses.

title: Iron-Catalyzed Stereoselective Glycosylation for Rapid Synthesis of Mucin-Type O-Linked Glycopeptide Core Structures 1 and 2
summary: Mucin-type glycopeptides and glycoproteins are the most prevalent type of <em>O</em>-linked glycosylation in eukaryotes. Many forms of cancer aberrantly express mucin-type glycopeptides and glycoproteins such as Tn-antigens and MUC1. These glycoconjugates have been extensively explored as viable biomarkers and therapeutic targets for CAR-T cell therapy and cancer vaccines. Due to the specific and selective nature of these therapies, a homogenous source of mucin-type glycopeptides and glycoproteins is required. Homogenous isolation of these compounds from natural sources is difficult due to their ubiquitous and complex expression across most epithelial cells. This positions chemical and enzymatic synthetic methods as powerful tools to access homogenous samples of mucin-type glycopeptides and glycoproteins. summary: Sermon 2 on the Eighth Sunday after the Holy Spirit was delivered by Dmitry of Rostov in the Holy Dormition Monastery of Alexandrova Sloboda at the beginning of the 18th century. title: A new critical edition cum catalogue of the Book of Architecture of John Thorpe
summary: The Book of Architecture of John Thorpe (c.1565-1655) consists of some 295 drawings ranging primarily from the 1590s to the 1620s and covering 168 buildings, mainly but not only English, and amongst the greatest of the period. The drawings include plans, elevations, some full-size sections of mouldings, and a depiction of the five orders derived from Hans Blum’s 1550 treatise on the orders. Bound in a hard cover in the 18th c., since 1810 the album has been preserved in one of London’s most iconic museums of British architecture, created by the celebrated architect Sir John Soane (1753-1837), who added to the album with about six sketches of his own. Alongside new catalogue entries featuring digital copies of the drawings in colour, enlargeable, and uncut, my edition will include a c.40.000-word critical analysis addressing all aspects above-mentioned. title: The Catholic liturgy as pedagogical reality
summary: In this presentation I explore the Catholic liturgy as ‘pedagogical reality’ – drawing on the writing of Romano Guardini, a key figure in the early 20th century (German) liturgical reform movement. summary: Drawing on a one-year ethnography in Shenzhen’s tech zone (2023-2024) composed of individual interviews, textual analysis, and participant observations, this thesis develops an interpretive phenomenological analysis of working time and temporalities situated in the post-socialist context of contemporary urban China. title: Active-Route Collatz Proof Package: Proof Concept, Review Manuscript, Lemma Stock, and Finite Verification Artifacts
summary: This is a documentation, cleanup, and review-orientation update. The active proof package has been substantially optimized and simplified. Large theorem-carrier files were pruned to their active review-route anchors, obsolete/off-route artifacts were removed, and the terminal pure-D finite-state obstruction is now carried by a compact algebraic low-bit obstruction lemma rather than the previous large FSM artifact. The update is intended to make the active proof route easier to follow for readers and reviewers: where to start, which files carry which proof obligations, how large lemma files should be navigated, and how finite audit artifacts relate to theorem-facing proof carriers. Recommended review entry points:- Reviewer_Overview.md- Proof_Concept.md- Proof_Map.md- ACTIVE/review/README_FOR_REVIEW.md- ACTIVE/review/dependency_matrix.md- ACTIVE/review/final_review_manuscript.md For questions, corrections, or review comments, contact: Jaan Allikverejaan@lahendus.ee

title: Sport Genetics Research in Turkey (2019–2026): A Scoping Review of Research Trends, Methodological Quality, and Future Directions
summary: This study aims to systematically review genetic association studies examining the relationship between genetic polymorphisms and athletic performance, injury risk, and psychological parameters in Turkish athlete populations. The review includes studies published between January 1, 2019 and April 1, 2026. Databases to be searched include PubMed, Web of Science, TRDizin, and DergiPark. The study follows PRISMA-ScR and PRISMA 2020 guidelines and includes methodological quality assessment using NIH and STREGA tools. Data synthesis will be conducted primarily using descriptive and comparative narrative analysis due to methodological heterogeneity across studies. The protocol is registered to ensure transparency, reproducibility, and methodological rigor.

title: The Amyloid Precursor Protein as a Universal Survival Molecule: A Critical Perspective on APP-Suppressing Therapies for Alzheimer's Disease
summary: Abstract The amyloid precursor protein (APP) is best known in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) research as the source of the neurotoxic amyloid-β (Aβ) peptide. Consequently, therapeutic strategies now entering clinical trials seek to reduce Aβ production by directly suppressing APP expression itself, most notably through RNA interference (RNAi). However, a growing body of evidence reveals that APP is not a passive substrate for pathology but a deeply conserved, pro-survival molecule deployed by the brain and body in response to every form of catastrophic insult—from synaptic fatigue and traumatic axonal injury to systemic wound healing and bone fracture. This manuscript argues that APP must be understood as a universal “connector” and “mender,” a molecule evolved to detect and bridge any disconnect that threatens the integrity of the nervous system. title: Framing the stage and staging the frame: Man's desire and fleeting beauty
summary: Frames, such as prologues and epilogues, are a common feature of early European drama. The rich variety of early theatre, its diversity of players, purpose and place, requires a nuanced investigation of its dramatic frames, but studies so far have tended to offer oversimplified accounts assuming merely practical and/or narrowly didactic functions. This scholarship is also generally based on read experiences of play scripts whereas, in fact, performance research and audience research are essential to an investigation of the effect of frames on audiences. By staging an early play with and without its frame and analysing audience feedback, we shed further light on the multifaceted effect of framing material for the performance and its reception and thus also on the didactic role of early drama.

authors: Alan Chamberlain, Sine Zambach, Mads Bødker, Maj Kullberg Øllgaard
summary: AI shifts musical creation by changing how performers and composers engage with instruments. Interviews with nine composers show three ways AI becomes embodied knowledge, moving resistance from physical effort to probabilistic navigation and reshaping affect and understanding.Composing and playing acoustic instruments demands embodied and cognitive investment; creating music with generative AI more often involves prompting, steering, and iterating outputs. Making with GenAI seldom feels like composing at an acoustic piano. title: Missing from the Mainstage: Disabled Musicians Access to Live Music Vennues In Glasgow
summary: Disabled musicians find Glasgow's live music venues inaccessible despite their access being enshrined in UN and UK legislation. As an UNESCO 'City of Music' and once European 'Capital of Culture', Glasgow acts as a unique but exemplarily case of intertwining physical, attitudinal, and legislative barriers. Recommendations produced by this research are built upon data analysis work with the Musicians Union, city-wide live music venue online information access mapping, and interviews with venue management teams, musicians who face access barriers, and those who work in the Glaswegian live music industries.

title: Embodied Interaction and Audio-Visuals in Performing Arts
summary: With the emergence of technologies for collecting data for the body, such as motion tracking and biosignal sensing, there has been an interest in using these technologies in performing arts. In such performance settings, this data has been mapped to different types of output, such as audio-visuals. In this chapter, we discuss the intersection of embodied interaction, performing arts and audio-visual practice. In particular, we will present two lines of work, one exploring audio-visuals in contemporary dance (the Moving Digits project) and another combining gesture, electronic music, and visuals (works by Atau Tanaka). From the analysis of these two lines of work and related projects, we map out the area of embodied interaction in performative audio-visual practice and identify relevant categories.

title: Override: An Experiment in Interrupting the Congruity of Audio-Visual Relationships Across Analogue and Digital Domains
summary: Override is an experimental mixed reality series designed to disrupt the usual fusion of sight and sound through using mobile phones and noise-cancelling headphones on double-decker buses. Participants experience visual journeys on the phone that are intentionally mismatched in directionality with accompanying sounds, while the actual motion and views from the bus introduce further complexity. The project leverages kinetic sensation to interrupt habitual sensory integration, highlighting the complexity of multisensory experience. This chapter draws on several theoretical perspectives to examine Override’s approach to understand how the brain integrates sensory signals. The concept of synchresis is discussed to understand how audio-visual signals tend to fuse spontaneously, and how this can be deliberately disrupted. Prepared source-data is intentionally not distributed in this record because it is large and reproducible from the raw resources. The intended use is to first rebuild the local source-data from resources-bundle.zip, and then optionally combine it with generated-artifacts-cache.zip to avoid rerunning the downstream workflow stages and to speed up figure regeneration.

summary: To live through a film festival is to live through an intensive emotive experience of film viewings, encounters with friends and strangers, travel, displacement and the exploration of new spaces – both real and imaginary. title: Roman Polanski after The Pianist: The Man and His Films
summary: Roman Polanski after The Pianist examines Polanski’s later films as a distinct and coherent phase in his career. Situating these works within changing industrial, cultural and political conditions, the book shows how Polanski’s late cinema rethinks genre, sound, work, domestic space and historical memory. Drawing on production studies, sound analysis and theories of authorship and mediation, it explores the formal strategies through which these films construct their cinematic worlds. Engaging contemporary debates on art, morality and authorship, the authors argue for the critical autonomy of artworks in a culture increasingly shaped by biographical scrutiny and moral judgement.

title: Grand Theft Auto: National Identity, Transnational Production, and the Ambivalent Politics of Play
summary: Grand Theft Auto (Rockstar Games, 1997-; GTA) occupies a unique position in the cultural and industrial history of digital games. Initially developed by DMA Design (Dundee, Scotland), and later Rockstar North (Edinburgh, Scotland) under the global brand of Rockstar Games, GTA is simultaneously a local product and a transnational cultural artefact. We argue that GTA operates as a liminal artefact of identity: Scottish in origin, British in sensibility, American in setting, and global in circulation. Through its production context, aesthetic strategies, and reception, the franchise demonstrates the complex interdependence of national identity and transnational media. Our paper contributes to discussions in game studies on national identity (Webber 2020; Wills 2019) and global production (Kerr, 2017).

summary: The adaptive reuse project for Old Brainerd Junior High School aims to transform the historically significant building into a space that better serves the community, as it once did. title: Historic preservation through adaptive reuse and wellness hospitality
summary: Hotel Bowman is an adaptive reuse boutique hotel located within the former Old Brainerd Junior High School in Chattanooga, Tennessee. The project reimagines the historic structure as a hospitality environment rooted in athletic legacy, community, and wellness. Blending preserved architectural character with contemporary interventions, the design honors the building’s past while introducing a new identity centered on performance and recovery. title: DNA as Resonant Engine
summary: This paper explains that DNA and the genetic code instantiate the same tetrad-cycle architectural family developed in the companion resonant-engine and Solar-System papers. At molecular scale, the paper assigns the four nucleotide families and genetic-code structure to a four-role architecture specified by Energetic First Principles (E1P). It presents DNA as a coherence-gradient system in which base chemistry, pairing, codon organization, chromatin structure, mutation dynamics, and phase-sensitive regulatory effects can be read through a common architectural vocabulary. The paper develops the molecular case for the Resonant Systems Program and provides falsifiable predictions involving mutation gradients, codon usage, phase-family preservation, G-quadruplex and i-motif behavior, chromatin organization, and liquid-liquid phase separation. This paper is Paper III of the first Resonant Systems program.

title: On Zaya (2025) – Marcel van Luit
summary: Abstract The Medium Betrayed the Miracle is a Post-Interpretive Criticism essay examining the encounter between image, memory, and medium through a detailed reading of Zaya’s digitally rendered allegorical tableau. What first appears to be a painting—replete with chiaroscuro, symbolic fauna, and mythic staging—gradually reveals itself as a digital work. This revelation becomes the fulcrum of the essay: a meditation on authenticity, labor, memory, and the ethics of medium. Through the tiger’s posture of grief, the zebra’s ecstatic witness, the birds’ opposing grammars of love, and the subtle fractures embedded in the architecture, the piece traces the tension between lived reality and stylized recollection. The discovery of its digital origin becomes not a dismissal but an invocation—forcing a confrontation with our inherited biases about materiality, struggle, and truth. title: The Emerging Political Actors in the Anthropocene: Cosmopolitics of the Earthbounds in Amitav Ghosh's Gun Island
summary: The present article seeks to engender a much-needed political ecocriticism for our time. In doing so, it draws on Bruno Latour's notions of the political subject/agent in the Anthropocene. Having done that, it proposes an extrapolated version of Latour's earthbounds as the new political actors in the Anthropocene. In conformity with Latour, the present author holds that "Earthbound" does not refer to an identity. Nor does it refer to structural subjectivity. According to me, it is an onto-political redescription of humans, subjected to the limits articulated by Planetary boundaries. In its essence, earth-bound names an ontology as well as a cosmopolitics of a concerned yet debating public. As an ontology it posits that, at present or in the near future, the earth offers no exit for earthlings, who, having left the pages of Science Fiction, have now acquired a new meaning, i.e., all living beings of the earth. title: Genesis of Organizational Innovation in Healthcare
authors: Sabrina Grandclaude, Didier Grandclaude, Thierry Nobre, Cadenza Academic Translations
summary: Based on the analysis of 96 organizational innovation in healthcare (OIH) projects and 52 interviews conducted with project leaders initiating these innovations, this research identifies the phenomena underlying the genesis of OIHs. The results highlight the major role played by factors such as patient empathy, international inspiration, academic inspiration, technological inspiration, serendipitous encounters, and the desire for organizational transformation in driving the generation of OIHs. Furthermore, our findings emphasize the dual nature of the research and development process for these innovations, characterized as both ex nihilo and ex materia.

summary: It is clear that naming deals that are the result of an agreement between a public authority and a company constitute a dynamic market in France, particularly in the sports sector (Sporsora, 2022). Indeed, no fewer than 18 such partnerships were signed in 2022, following the 14 concluded in 2021. At the same time, there is a growing body of research dedicated to this subject. This work mainly examines the benefits that naming can bring to a sponsoring brand (Marousseau, 2009). However, the benefits of naming for local authorities remain unexplored (Walliser, 2006), even though the latter are increasingly resorting to naming of their public facilities with a view to limiting public spending (Séguin, 2008, Brameret, 2019). title: Combining Foresight Narratives and Serious Games to Codevelop Adaptive Water Management Pathways
authors: Nina Graveline, Juliette Le Gallo, Alexandre Alix, Marta Debolini, David Dorchies, Katrin Erdlenbruch, Sébastien Loubier
summary: In the Mediterranean area, climate change threatens both farming and water resources. The need for methods to support reflection and dialogue on transformational adaptation strategies is urgent. We propose and demonstrate an innovative approach, co-constructing pathways for climate change adaptation and water management by combining (i) participative scenario building and (ii) a serious game. While the first explores the combination of exogenous driving forces on the agricultural system consistent with SSPs at regional level, the serious game allows us to explore the co-evolution of land and water use and related policies at the farm level. Results confirm that land use can vary greatly in a medium-term horizon. Our approach helps to envision the role of land use and diversification in future water demand under climate change. The results show that the effect of land use changes on water demand is much higher than the effect of climate scenarios. JEL Codes: B4, B5, O3, Q1, Q2

title: Genèse de l’Innovation Organisationnelle en Santé
authors: Sabrina Grandclaude, Didier Grandclaude, Thierry Nobre
summary: Prenant appui sur l’analyse de 96 projets d’innovations organisationnelles en santé (IOS) et sur la conduite de 52 entretiens auprès de porteurs de projet à l’initiative de ces innovations, cette recherche identifie les phénomènes à la genèse des IOS. Les résultats montrent ainsi le rôle majeur joué par des phénomènes tels que l’empathie patient, l’inspiration internationale, l’inspiration académique, l’inspiration technologique, les effets de rencontre et la volonté de transformation organisationnelle dans la génération des IOS. Par ailleurs, nos résultats soulignent également le caractère ex nihilo et ex materia du processus de recherche et de développement de ces innovations.

title: Political Uncertainty and Firm-Level Stock Market Reactions in the United States
summary: Political uncertainty has become an increasingly important feature of the global economy, with major geopolitical events often triggering rapid reactions in financial markets. This study examines how geopolitical shocks affect firm-level stock market performance in the United States. Using an event study framework, the analysis evaluates cumulative returns and stock return volatility for fourteen publicly traded firms across nine major geopolitical events between 2016 and 2022, including the Brexit referendum, the U.S.–China trade war, the COVID-19 pandemic, and the Russia–Ukraine war. The results indicate that most firms experienced negative abnormal returns around geopolitical events, suggesting that political uncertainty is generally perceived by investors as a negative shock to firm valuation. title: 2026 Sub-Librarians Meeting: Vincent Starrett: Cataloger, Collector, and Unwilling Seller of Libraries
summary: Fans of Sherlock Holmes will be delighted to learn the Sub-Librarians Scion of the Baker Street Irregulars are hosting their 48th meeting at the American Library Association. The Scion welcomes researcher Philip Cunningham to talk about the famous writer, newspaperman, bibliophile, and Sherlockian: Vincent Starrett. The presentation will focus on Starrett's connections to libraries including the creation of book catalogs for Frank Morris, Walter Hill, and David Randall. Cunningham will also discuss his research in creating a detailed timeline chronicling the 31,848 days of Starrett's life and preparing an annotated edition of Born in a Bookshop, Starrett's bibliographical memoir. Philip Cunningham, a former Chief Steward of Torists (2014-2018), became interested in Vincent Starrett in 2007. He was given the investiture "Abe Slaney" in the Baker Street Irregulars in 2013.

title: Platforming threatoric on TikTok : racial‑religious fear during Malaysia’s 15th general election
summary: This paper examines how TikTok shaped the production and circulation of threatoric, the affective and discursive staging of racial and religious threat, during Malaysia’s 15th General Election (GE15). title: Que tus ojos no se cansen de brillar
summary: Que tus ojos no se cansen de brillar is a nine-song song cycle for soprano, saxophone, clarinet, percussion, electric guitar, violin, viola, and cello. Setting texts by Giannina Braschi alongside selected poems by Ángela María Dávila, Julia de Burgos, and Pedro Pietri, the work explores Puertorriqueñidad through musical hybridity. Drawing on Puerto Rican musical traditions and the island’s diasporic experience as core structural elements, the cycle constantly shifts styles, weaving together lyrical, experimental, and vernacular elements to reflect the resilience, fragmentation, and diversity of Puerto Rican identity across its literary, musical and experiential voices.

title: The Transformative Potential of the Beauty Industry: From Visual Aesthetics to the Psychological Restoration of the Individual
summary: The beauty industry is evolving from a focus on visual enhancement toward a multidimensional system that supports psychological restoration and identity formation. The aim of this study is to analyze the transformative potential of aesthetic practices in improving individual well-being. Methods include a systematic review of recent interdisciplinary studies and comparative analysis of aesthetic and psycho-emotional outcomes. Results indicate that modern beauty practices—such as skincare programs, makeup, and hairstyling—significantly influence self-esteem, emotional stability, and social integration. Furthermore, the integration of digital technologies and personalized approaches enhances these effects. The findings confirm that the beauty industry functions not only as a commercial sector but also as a socio-cultural and therapeutic mechanism, contributing to holistic personal development and psychological resilience in contemporary society.

summary: This article reconstructs the biography and academic and social activities of Archpriest Alexander Mikhailovich Ivantsov-Platonov, one of the most signifi cant representatives of the Russian Church history in the second half of the 19th century. Despite Ivantsov-Platonov’s signifi cant infl uence on the development of university teaching in church history and theological thought, his biography has not been a topic of a comprehensive study. Special attention is paid to the intellectual evolution of the scholar, his relations with the Slavophiles, his role in the rapprochement of church and secular science, and his methodological diff erences with representatives of theological- academic historiography. title: The sounds of branding. Studying sonic distinctiveness in modern society
summary: The sonic dimension of branding has become an increasingly pervasive element of contemporary auditory experience. Strategically arranged auditory cues – establishing associative links with specific organizations and their offerings – are activated through engagement with a wide range of consumer products and promotional settings, from beverages and automobiles to retail spaces and media environments. As such, branding sounds significantly shape the affective and semiotic contours of consumer culture. Despite their ubiquity and influence, sound branding remains insufficiently understood from a scholarly perspective. Building on these premises, this book offers the first cohesive and comprehensive scholarly introduction to the sounds of branding. It explores what characterizes branding sounds and how and why they possess the capacity to shape perceptions, emotions, and interactions with organizations and their offerings. title: Raymond Williams and Structures of Feeling
summary: Raymond Williams is one of the most important anglophone cultural critics of the twentieth century. In a distinguished career, his readings of the British literary canon offered radical new ways of looking at British society as it developed from the Romantic period into the modern age. Central to this reevaluation was the idea of ‘structures of feeling’, which Williams shaped in order to explain the ways in which members of societies felt about one another, and how they changed over time. The authors of the present volume examine the idea of structures of feeling, and its value for ongoing contemporary debates about relationships of human feeling in areas such as anthropology, economics, law, literary studies, philosophy, psychology and social geography.
